origin.brief:
# Build: auto-recover-stuck-builds

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-13T11:45:11.111Z
> Brett: if anything stops working, the server/orchestrator fixes it automatically with no one asking. Detect builds marked running with no live session (killed exit 143, failed exit 1), reset and requeue them, retry failed sessions, keep every slot filled, FYI to phone per fix.

## What to build
Continue build "Auto-recover stuck builds" (auto-recover-stuck-builds) — Phase 1, model Fable.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-13 11:45):
"Brett: if anything stops working, the server/orchestrator fixes it automatically with no one asking. Detect builds marked running with no live session (killed exit 143, failed exit 1), reset and requeue them, retry failed sessions, keep every slot filled, FYI to phone per fix."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 10 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next. Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (2 left, ~20 min):
[ ] s1 (~10 min) Define the build-recovery@1 contract in framework/core/build-recovery.mjs. It covers: (1) the stuck states a build can be in (running with no live session, session killed with exit 143, session failed with exit 1, heartbeat stale, slot leaked); (2) what happens for each state (reset the step, requeue, retry the session, or park in Pending once the retry cap is reached); (3) the per-build retry counter and its backoff; (4) the recovery event record (build id, phase, cause, exit code, action, attempt, at); (5) a pure plan(builds, sessions, slots, now) function that returns actions and never runs side effects. Add the matching recovery fields to the builds@1 normaliser (normBuild keeps them), with a migration that defaults old records.
[ ] s2 (~10 min) Write golden fixtures and a checker for build-recovery@1. Cover each stuck state, the retry cap, backoff timing, a build whose live session is healthy (no action), and a build whose PR is merged (never requeued). Run the checker in the spec sweep.
Read first: framework/core/build-recovery.mjs, framework/core/build-pipeline.mjs, framework/core/builds-store-schema.mjs, framework/schemas/build-recovery.json, framework/spec/fixtures/build-recovery.json, framework/spec/check-build-recovery.mjs
Tick each step right after its commit: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step auto-recover-stuck-builds <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link auto-recover-stuck-builds --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account mossesx-max- for the Fable phase. Work through every step of the phase in this one session: they are checkpoints, not separate tasks. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step auto-recover-stuck-builds <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note auto-recover-stuck-builds "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

split.note: Split by Claude into 15 steps (2 Fable).

steps.text: Define the build-recovery@1 contract in framework/core/build-recovery.mjs. It covers: (1) the stuck states a build can be in (running with no live session, session killed with exit 143, session failed with exit 1, heartbeat stale, slot leaked); (2) what happens for each state (reset the step, requeue, retry the session, or park in Pending once the retry cap is reached); (3) the per-build retry counter and its backoff; (4) the recovery event record (build id, phase, cause, exit code, action, attempt, at); (5) a pure plan(builds, sessions, slots, now) function that returns actions and never runs side effects. Add the matching recovery fields to the builds@1 normaliser (normBuild keeps them), with a migration that defaults old records.
steps.why: New cross-surface contract and a builds@1 schema and migration change that the dispatcher, launcher and console all read

steps.text: Write golden fixtures and a checker for build-recovery@1. Cover each stuck state, the retry cap, backoff timing, a build whose live session is healthy (no action), and a build whose PR is merged (never requeued). Run the checker in the spec sweep.
steps.why: These fixtures are the conformance contract for the recovery planner

steps.text: Record the exit status of every headless session. claude-headless.sh traps the exit and writes the exit code, the signal (143 = SIGTERM), the end time and the account into a session status file under the agent-slots dir. It also writes a heartbeat file while the session runs, so the planner has real liveness data.

Add a session liveness reader in framework/cli/session-liveness.mjs. It joins the builds store's running builds with live PIDs, heartbeats, tmux sessions and the exit records from the previous step. It outputs the input that build-recovery plan() expects. Add a CLI: `session-liveness.mjs list --json`.

Add the recovery executor in apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/recover.mjs. It applies plan() actions through the builds store under its lock: set the stuck step back to todo, set status to queued with a recovery note, increment the retry counter, release leaked agent slots, and park the build in Pending with a reason once the cap is hit. It journals every action and publishes through builds-live.mjs. Add `--dry-run`.

Wire recovery into the dispatcher. pipeline.mjs tick runs recover first on every tick, then fills every free agent slot from the Queue (loop until slots or the Queue run out, not one build per tick), and respects account and model routing. The axf-pipeline cron needs no change.

Retry failed sessions on another worker. When the exit record shows a usage limit or an account error, the executor requeues the build with an account hint, so the dispatcher routes it to a different worker through claude-workers.mjs route.

Send an FYI to the phone for each fix. Declare a `build-recovered` notification type and a `build-recovery-parked` notification type in the plugin's notify.json. Send each one through axf.notify@1 (AmberX app) as one plain line: what stuck, the exit code, what was done and the attempt number. Parked builds get a banner item instead of only a push.

Register a systems-check health@1 check, `builds-stuck`, with an auto-fix that runs recover. Under the Fix it yourself setting it defaults to on. It turns red only when a build is parked after the cap or when recovery itself fails.

Add Recovery settings to the Build orchestrator settings sub-tab, on framework controls: auto-recover on/off, max retries (default 3), stale heartbeat minutes, backoff, FYI per fix on/off. Include the settings level-toolbar entries. Store them as Claude settings keys under builds.recovery.*.

Add a Recovery log view in the Build orchestrator: the latest recovery events per build (cause, exit, action, attempt) and a PriorityTag on each row. Each build view shows a recovery badge. Use only tokens and framework controls (DataGrid, TabGroup).

API parity for the Recovery log and settings. REST routes: GET /recovery (state, events, settings), POST /recovery/run (with dry_run), POST /recovery/settings, POST /recovery/retry/<id>, POST /recovery/park/<id>. Expose the same routes as MCP plugin commands. Add a console_show deep link target `builds/orchestrator/recovery`. Add the CLI `recover.mjs status|run|retry|park|settings` and voice actions `recovery.run`, `recovery.status` and `recovery.retry` for AmberX.

Write tests: run the executor against a temp builds store with fake exit records (143, 1, a stale heartbeat, a healthy session, the cap reached). Assert requeue, reset, slot release, park and notify calls, check that the tick fills all free slots, and run the routes smoke test. Add them to CI.

Lifecycle and docs: add uninstall coverage for the new data files, lifecycle markers, help and glossary descriptions for the new commands and settings, and a feature in the Shipped features ledger. Run plugin-lifecycle check, catalog.mjs --check and check-theme/check-controls/check-toolbars/check-chrome-assets.

Submit the Recovery log and settings to UI Review with 3 options and shots. Run the full checks. Write the report _claude/builds/reports/auto-recover-stuck-builds.md, covering what was added, the stuck states handled and how each part is reached through deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice. Add the THREADS.md row, open the PR stating API reach, link the PR with builds-live.mjs, and add the PR to the merge queue.

Docs: help entries and glossary descriptions for the new actions, CLI and MCP tools; _claude/memory/docs/console-control.md; a CLAUDE.md conventions line.

REST routes: GET /recovery (state, events, settings), POST /recovery/run (with dry_run), POST /recovery/settings, POST /recovery/retry/<id>, POST /recovery/park/<id>. It covers: (1) the stuck states a build can be in (running with no live session, session killed with exit 143, session failed with exit 1, heartbeat stale, slot leaked); (2) what happens for each state (reset the step, requeue, retry the session, or park in Pending once the retry cap is reached); (3) the per-build retry counter and its backoff; (4) the recovery event record (build id, phase, cause, exit code, action, attempt, at); (5) a pure plan(builds, sessions, slots, now) function that returns actions and never runs side effects. Add the matching recovery fields to the builds@1 normaliser (normBuild keeps them), with a migration that defaults old records.
[ ] s2 (~10 min) Write golden fixtures and a checker for build-recovery@1. Cover each stuck state, the retry cap, backoff timing, a build whose live session is healthy (no action), and a build whose PR is merged (never requeued). Run the checker in the spec sweep.

steps.text: Define the build-recovery@1 contract in framework/core/build-recovery.mjs. It covers: (1) the stuck states a build can be in (running with no live session, session killed with exit 143, session failed with exit 1, heartbeat stale, slot leaked); (2) what happens for each state (reset the step, requeue, retry the session, or park in Pending once the retry cap is reached); (3) the per-build retry counter and its backoff; (4) the recovery event record (build id, phase, cause, exit code, action, attempt, at); (5) a pure plan(builds, sessions, slots, now) function that returns actions and never runs side effects. steps.text: Write golden fixtures and a checker for build-recovery@1. Cover each stuck state, the retry cap, backoff timing, a build whose live session is healthy (no action), and a build whose PR is merged (never requeued). Run the checker in the spec sweep.
steps.why: These fixtures are the conformance contract for the recovery planner

steps.text: Record the exit status of every headless session. claude-headless.sh traps the exit and writes the exit code, the signal (143 = SIGTERM), the end time and the account into a session status file under the agent-slots dir. It also writes a heartbeat file while the session runs, so the planner has real liveness data.

Add a session liveness reader in framework/cli/session-liveness.mjs. It joins the builds store's running builds with live PIDs, heartbeats, tmux sessions and the exit records from the previous step. It outputs the input that build-recovery plan() expects. Add a CLI: `session-liveness.mjs list --json`.

Add the recovery executor in apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/recover.mjs. It applies plan() actions through the builds store under its lock: set the stuck step back to todo, set status to queued with a recovery note, increment the retry counter, release leaked agent slots, and park the build in Pending with a reason once the cap is hit. It journals every action and publishes through builds-live.mjs. Add `--dry-run`.

Wire recovery into the dispatcher. pipeline.mjs tick runs recover first on every tick, then fills every free agent slot from the Queue (loop until slots or the Queue run out, not one build per tick), and respects account and model routing. The axf-pipeline cron needs no change.

Retry failed sessions on another worker. When the exit record shows a usage limit or an account error, the executor requeues the build with an account hint, so the dispatcher routes it to a different worker through claude-workers.mjs route.

Send an FYI to the phone for each fix. Declare a `build-recovered` notification type and a `build-recovery-parked` notification type in the plugin's notify.json. Send each one through axf.notify@1 (AmberX app) as one plain line: what stuck, the exit code, what was done and the attempt number. Parked builds get a banner item instead of only a push.

Register a systems-check health@1 check, `builds-stuck`, with an auto-fix that runs recover. Under the Fix it yourself setting it defaults to on. It turns red only when a build is parked after the cap or when recovery itself fails.

Add Recovery settings to the Build orchestrator settings sub-tab, on framework controls: auto-recover on/off, max retries (default 3), stale heartbeat minutes, backoff, FYI per fix on/off. Include the settings level-toolbar entries. Store them as Claude settings keys under builds.recovery.*.

Add a Recovery log view in the Build orchestrator: the latest recovery events per build (cause, exit, action, attempt) and a PriorityTag on each row. Each build view shows a recovery badge. Use only tokens and framework controls (DataGrid, TabGroup).

API parity for the Recovery log and settings. REST routes: GET /recovery (state, events, settings), POST /recovery/run (with dry_run), POST /recovery/settings, POST /recovery/retry/<id>, POST /recovery/park/<id>. Expose the same routes as MCP plugin commands. Add a console_show deep link target `builds/orchestrator/recovery`. Add the CLI `recover.mjs status|run|retry|park|settings` and voice actions `recovery.run`, `recovery.status` and `recovery.retry` for AmberX.

Run plugin-lifecycle check, catalog.mjs --check and check-theme/check-controls/check-toolbars/check-chrome-assets.

Submit the Recovery log and settings to UI Review with 3 options and shots. Run the full checks. Write the report _claude/builds/reports/auto-recover-stuck-builds.md, covering what was added, the stuck states handled and how each part is reached through deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice. Add the THREADS.md row, open the PR stating API reach, link the PR with builds-live.mjs, and add the PR to the merge queue.

# Build: combine-merge-queue-into-one-pr

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-13T11:55:36.143Z
> Brett: stop merging one at a time and in order. Take every PR in the merge queue that's done building (#560, #562, #563, #564, #566, #568, #570, #513, #515, #529, #539, #544, #545, plus #556 if ready), combine them all into ONE branch, pull in main, fix every conflict and failing check, open one PR and merge it now. Confirm the merge on GitHub, close the originals as merged-via-combined, redeploy. Fix whatever needs fixing; don't stop to ask.

## What to build
Continue build "Combine merge queue into one PR" (combine-merge-queue-into-one-pr) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-13 11:55):
"Brett: stop merging one at a time and in order. Take every PR in the merge queue that's done building (#560, #562, #563, #564, #566, #568, #570, #513, #515, #529, #539, #544, #545, plus #556 if ready), combine them all into ONE branch, pull in main, fix every conflict and failing check, open one PR and merge it now. Confirm the merge on GitHub, close the originals as merged-via-combined, redeploy. Fix whatever needs fixing; don't stop to ask."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 10 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next. Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. CLI: confirm <repo> <pr> [--wait], status <repo> <pr>, list.

Persistent pending-confirmation store + poller: record each merge call as pending-github-confirmation in the push-banner data dir, a tick that re-reads pending ones with backoff, flips them to merged or merge-unconfirmed after the timeout, and raises one health@1 banner item for unconfirmed merges.

Merge queue path: after each queue merge call, record pending-github-confirmation and only mark the stack entry merged (and trigger the one-per-stack redeploy) once merge-confirm says merged; unconfirmed entries stay in the queue as 'awaiting GitHub'.

Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 10 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next. Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.

Define one address grammar for screen, tab, sub-tab, setting, button, function, plugin, grid row and build step (e.g. view:builds/tab:pipeline/grid:queue/row:<id>). Define the verbs open, state, press, set, scroll (up/down/page/top/bottom/to), focus, search, plugin.enable and plugin.disable. Write it up in framework/spec/CONSOLE-CONTROL.md.
[ ] s2 (~8 min) Add the console-control@1 JSON schema (address, command, result and state shapes) to framework/schemas, and regenerate the JSON Schemas with axf.mjs schemas.
[ ] s3 (~10 min) Write the reference engine framework/core/engines/console-control.ts. It parses and formats addresses, validates commands against the schema, resolves an address against a target registry snapshot, and returns typed errors with stable wire codes.
[ ] s4 (~8 min) Add golden fixtures for console-control (parsing, resolving, errors and scroll maths) to gen-fixtures.mts and a check script. Record the Kotlin twin as a deferred gap in PORTING.md (Android on hold).
[ ] s5 (~10 min) Add the framework target registry framework/react/controlTargets.ts: a useControlTarget hook and a data-axf-target convention. Buttons, tabs, settings and views register their address, label, keywords and an invoke/get/set handler. AxfProvider installs the registry.
[ ] s6 (~10 min) Wire TabGroup, Button and the settings rows to register targets automatically, using their existing settings ids and labels as addresses, so most of the UI is addressable with no per-view code.
[ ] s7 (~8 min) Add the scroll contract framework/react/scrollControl.ts. It finds the active or named scroll container and runs scroll up/down/page/top/bottom/to-address, and reports the scroll position and extent as state.
[ ] s8 (~10 min) Grid and table focus: DataGrid and the build step lists register every row and step as a target. focus(address) scrolls the row into view, selects it, highlights it through theme tokens (opacityTint) and works on virtualised rows.

steps.text: Define the build-recovery@1 contract in framework/core/build-recovery.mjs. It covers: (1) the stuck states a build can be in (running with no live session, session killed with exit 143, session failed with exit 1, heartbeat stale, slot leaked); (2) what happens for each state (reset the step, requeue, retry the session, or park in Pending once the retry cap is reached); (3) the per-build retry counter and its backoff; (4) the recovery event record (build id, phase, cause, exit code, action, attempt, at); (5) a pure plan(builds, sessions, slots, now) function that returns actions and never runs side effects. Add the matching recovery fields to the builds@1 normaliser (normBuild keeps them), with a migration that defaults old records.

steps.text: Write golden fixtures and a checker for build-recovery@1. Cover each stuck state, the retry cap, backoff timing, a build whose live session is healthy (no action), and a build whose PR is merged (never requeued). Run the checker in the spec sweep.

steps.text: Record the exit status of every headless session. claude-headless.sh traps the exit and writes the exit code, the signal (143 = SIGTERM), the end time and the account into a session status file under the agent-slots dir. Send an FYI to the phone for each fix. Declare a `build-recovered` notification type and a `build-recovery-parked` notification type in the plugin's notify.json. Send each one through axf.notify@1 (AmberX app) as one plain line: what stuck, the exit code, what was done and the attempt number. Parked builds get a banner item instead of only a push.

Add a Recovery log view in the Build orchestrator: the latest recovery events per build (cause, exit, action, attempt) and a PriorityTag on each row. Each build view shows a recovery badge. Use only tokens and framework controls (DataGrid, TabGroup).

API parity for the Recovery log and settings. REST routes: GET /recovery (state, events, settings), POST /recovery/run (with dry_run), POST /recovery/settings, POST /recovery/retry/<id>, POST /recovery/park/<id>. Expose the same routes as MCP plugin commands. Add a console_show deep link target `builds/orchestrator/recovery`. Add the CLI `recover.mjs status|run|retry|park|settings` and voice actions `recovery.run`, `recovery.status` and `recovery.retry` for AmberX.

Write tests: run the executor against a temp builds store with fake exit records (143, 1, a stale heartbeat, a healthy session, the cap reached). Assert requeue, reset, slot release, park and notify calls, check that the tick fills all free slots, and run the routes smoke test. Add them to CI.

steps.text: Define the build-recovery@1 contract in framework/core/build-recovery.mjs. Add the matching recovery fields to the builds@1 normaliser (normBuild keeps them), with a migration that defaults old records.
steps.why: New cross-surface contract and a builds@1 schema and migration change that the dispatcher, launcher and console all read

steps.text: Write golden fixtures and a checker for build-recovery@1. Cover each stuck state, the retry cap, backoff timing, a build whose live session is healthy (no action), and a build whose PR is merged (never requeued). Run the checker in the spec sweep.

steps.text: Record the exit status of every headless session. claude-headless.sh traps the exit and writes the exit code, the signal (143 = SIGTERM), the end time and the account into a session status file under the agent-slots dir. REST routes: GET /recovery (state, events, settings), POST /recovery/run (with dry_run), POST /recovery/settings, POST /recovery/retry/<id>, POST /recovery/park/<id>. It covers: (1) the stuck states a build can be in (running with no live session, session killed with exit 143, session failed with exit 1, heartbeat stale, slot leaked); (2) what happens for each state (reset the step, requeue, retry the session, or park in Pending once the retry cap is reached); (3) the per-build retry counter and its backoff; (4) the recovery event record (build id, phase, cause, exit code, action, attempt, at); (5) a pure plan(builds, sessions, slots, now) function that returns actions and never runs side effects. Add the matching recovery fields to the builds@1 normaliser (normBuild keeps them), with a migration that defaults old records.
steps.why: New cross-surface contract and a builds@1 schema and migration change that the dispatcher, launcher and console all read

steps.text: Write golden fixtures and a checker for build-recovery@1. Cover each stuck state, the retry cap, backoff timing, a build whose live session is healthy (no action), and a build whose PR is merged (never requeued). Run the checker in the spec sweep.
steps.why: These fixtures are the conformance contract for the recovery planner

steps.text: Record the exit status of every headless session. claude-headless.sh traps the exit and writes the exit code, the signal (143 = SIGTERM), the end time and the account into a session status file under the agent-slots dir. It also writes a heartbeat file while the session runs, so the planner has real liveness data.

Add a session liveness reader in framework/cli/session-liveness.mjs. It joins the builds store's running builds with live PIDs, heartbeats, tmux sessions and the exit records from the previous step. It outputs the input that build-recovery plan() expects. Add a CLI: `session-liveness.mjs list --json`.

Add the recovery executor in apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/recover.mjs. It applies plan() actions through the builds store under its lock: set the stuck step back to todo, set status to queued with a recovery note, increment the retry counter, release leaked agent slots, and park the build in Pending with a reason once the cap is hit. It journals every action and publishes through builds-live.mjs. Add `--dry-run`.

Wire recovery into the dispatcher. pipeline.mjs tick runs recover first on every tick, then fills every free agent slot from the Queue (loop until slots or the Queue run out, not one build per tick), and respects account and model routing. The axf-pipeline cron needs no change.

Retry failed sessions on another worker. When the exit record shows a usage limit or an account error, the executor requeues the build with an account hint, so the dispatcher routes it to a different worker through claude-workers.mjs route.

Send an FYI to the phone for each fix. Declare a `build-recovered` notification type and a `build-recovery-parked` notification type in the plugin's notify.json. Send each one through axf.notify@1 (AmberX app) as one plain line: what stuck, the exit code, what was done and the attempt number. Parked builds get a banner item instead of only a push.

Register a systems-check health@1 check, `builds-stuck`, with an auto-fix that runs recover. Under the Fix it yourself setting it defaults to on. It turns red only when a build is parked after the cap or when recovery itself fails.

Add Recovery settings to the Build orchestrator settings sub-tab, on framework controls: auto-recover on/off, max retries (default 3), stale heartbeat minutes, backoff, FYI per fix on/off. Include the settings level-toolbar entries. Store them as Claude settings keys under builds.recovery.*.

Add a Recovery log view in the Build orchestrator: the latest recovery events per build (cause, exit, action, attempt) and a PriorityTag on each row. Each build view shows a recovery badge. Use only tokens and framework controls (DataGrid, TabGroup).

API parity for the Recovery log and settings. REST routes: GET /recovery (state, events, settings), POST /recovery/run (with dry_run), POST /recovery/settings, POST /recovery/retry/<id>, POST /recovery/park/<id>. Expose the same routes as MCP plugin commands. Add a console_show deep link target `builds/orchestrator/recovery`. Add the CLI `recover.mjs status|run|retry|park|settings` and voice actions `recovery.run`, `recovery.status` and `recovery.retry` for AmberX.

Write tests: run the executor against a temp builds store with fake exit records (143, 1, a stale heartbeat, a healthy session, the cap reached). Assert requeue, reset, slot release, park and notify calls, check that the tick fills all free slots, and run the routes smoke test. Add them to CI.

Lifecycle and docs: add uninstall coverage for the new data files, lifecycle markers, help and glossary descriptions for the new commands and settings, and a feature in the Shipped features ledger. Run plugin-lifecycle check, catalog.mjs --check and check-theme/check-controls/check-toolbars/check-chrome-assets.

Submit the Recovery log and settings to UI Review with 3 options and shots. Run the full checks. Write the report _claude/builds/reports/auto-recover-stuck-builds.md, covering what was added, the stuck states handled and how each part is reached through deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice. Add the THREADS.md row, open the PR stating API reach, link the PR with builds-live.mjs, and add the PR to the merge queue.

CLI: add axf console do|state|targets|search|focus|scroll|plugin enable|disable to framework/cli/axf.mjs, calling the REST routes, with --json output.

Voice (AmberX): map phrases to console-control commands ('scroll down', 'open plugins settings', 'find <x>', 'show step 3 of <build>', 'disable plugin <y>', 'press <button>') through the console actions registry, with spoken confirmation of the result.
control@1 integration: register the console-control targets so that control@1 tokens and planner items can point at addresses, and add console actions console.control.* with descriptions.

Search palette UI: a framework command-palette (Ctrl+K or a banner chip) listing search hits. Picking one pulls it into focus. Use tokens and TabGroup/Button only. Its API is the search route: deep link ?axf-cmd=search&q=, state via console_control_state.
Backfill batch 1: add data-axf-target and settings ids to hand-drawn elements in the banner, nav, Settings and Terminal views that the framework hooks don't reach.
Backfill batch 2: Builds views (orchestrator, Pipeline, Pending, Queue, Build manager), so that every build row and step is focusable.
Backfill batch 3: the remaining plugin UIs (UI Review, Plan Studio, Breakroom, Shipped features, Glossary and others) and their grids.

Coverage CI check framework/cli/check-console-control.mjs. It fails when a view, tab group, toolbar, setting, plugin or DataGrid has no address. The ratchet baseline framework/spec/console-control-baseline.json can only go down. Wire it into CI.

Executor tests: Playwright against vite preview. Open a tab, scroll, focus a grid row and a build step, set a setting, press a button and search-then-focus, asserting the reported state.
Parity test: the same command through REST, MCP, CLI and the voice intent gives identical results and state.
Docs: help entries and glossary descriptions for the new actions, CLI and MCP tools; _claude/memory/docs/console-control.md; a CLAUDE.md conventions line.

Run all the checks (fixtures, check-console-control, theme, controls, toolbars, chrome-assets, pytest, e2e, parity). Write the report _claude/builds/reports/full-api-and-voice-control-of-the-entire-console-every-tab-screen-setting-bu.md, add a THREADS.md row and open the PR stating how each feature is reached (deep link, state, actions, settings via REST, MCP, CLI and voice).

Button and function inventory: expose the existing console action registry, toolbar buttons and context-menu items as press targets. Destructive ones need an explicit confirm flag, and deciding actions (approve/deny) stay personOnly.

Plugin targets: address every plugin, its UI and settings tab, and add enable/disable through the plugin-manager engine. Report dependency effects (what needs it) in the result. Core plugins refuse disable with a reason.

Search index: one ranked search over screens, tabs, settings, buttons, plugins, help and everything currently loaded (grid rows, build steps, UI Review items, chat lines). Each hit carries its address so it can be pulled into focus.

Console screen and tab inventory: build a static index of every console view, nav entry and tab group, with addresses, labels and keywords, from the view registry, and export it for the server.

Settings inventory: every setting in the SettingsRegistry and in every plugin sub-tab gets an address with get/set and type and range validation. Owner-only Claude settings are marked personOnly and refused.

Button and function inventory: expose the existing console action registry, toolbar buttons and context-menu items as press targets. Destructive ones need an explicit confirm flag, and deciding actions (approve/deny) stay personOnly.

Plugin targets: address every plugin, its UI and settings tab, and add enable/disable through the plugin-manager engine. Report dependency effects (what needs it) in the result. Core plugins refuse disable with a reason.

Search index: one ranked search over screens, tabs, settings, buttons, plugins, help and everything currently loaded (grid rows, build steps, UI Review items, chat lines). Each hit carries its address so it can be pulled into focus.

Browser executor: the console page receives console-control commands over the existing relay channel and runs open/press/set/scroll/focus/search through the target registry. It highlights the result and returns a result plus a live state snapshot (screen, tab, scroll, focused row).

Commands go to the open console session (Follow Amber channel), with a clear 'no console open' error and an open_url fallback link. Settings and plugin toggles that need no browser run server-side.

Server-side guards: personOnly and owner-only refusal, confirm for destructive actions, an audit log line per command, and a rate limit. Send veto-policy tags to axHub for state-changing verbs and leave navigation read-only.
MCP tools in mcp_server.py: console_control_targets, _state, _do, _search, _focus, _scroll and _plugin (enable/disable). Extend console_show/console_open to accept the new addresses.
CLI: add axf console do|state|targets|search|focus|scroll|plugin enable|disable to framework/cli/axf.mjs, calling the REST routes, with --json output.

Voice (AmberX): map phrases to console-control commands ('scroll down', 'open plugins settings', 'find <x>', 'show step 3 of <build>', 'disable plugin <y>', 'press <button>') through the console actions registry, with spoken confirmation of the result.
control@1 integration: register the console-control targets so that control@1 tokens and planner items can point at addresses, and add console actions console.control.* with descriptions.

Search palette UI: a framework command-palette (Ctrl+K or a banner chip) listing search hits. Picking one pulls it into focus. Use tokens and TabGroup/Button only. Its API is the search route: deep link ?axf-cmd=search&q=, state via console_control_state.

before.title: Orchestrator checks Shipped features before splitting any job
before.detail: When the orchestrator receives a job and splits it into steps, it first checks the Shipped features ledger (which must hold every feature the orchestrator has ever built). It must: not build anything twice; not break or redo anything already done; and if a step would conflict with or change something already built, notify Brett (AmberX notification) and wait before going on. Make the Shipped features ledger complete (backfill every landed build) and keep it updated on every land. Also standing rule: ONLY the orchestrator launches builds, picks model and account, owns pending/queue and monitors status; voice/chat sessions only hand it requests.

notes.text: Conflict flow (Brett): a conflicting step is moved to a special Conflicts section and removed from the build; the other steps still build. Brett gets an AmberX notification-panel item that explains the conflict and offers suggested resolutions; he taps a suggestion or types a prompt, which goes to the orchestrator, and the orchestrator makes a new build from it. Then test it: Brett will send a 3-4 step build that deliberately overlaps existing shipped features to confirm the orchestrator catches it.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

Brett (Nov 9): "needs a way to go through all the pending builds and the build queue and search for steps that are gonna break existing work or conflict with it, or it's already done, or it doesn't need it anymore." Add a Sweep: a button on the builds page (and API/voice: 'sweep the builds') plus an automatic run on every land. It checks every step of every pending and queued build against the Shipped features ledger, main's code, and the other pending/queued builds, and flags each step: Already done (shipped by build X), Conflicts (would change/break feature Y, shows the files and lines), Duplicate (same as a step in build Z), Obsolete (no longer needed: superseded or its target was removed), OK. Results: badges on each build and step, a Sweep report with a filter per flag, and one-tap fixes per flag: drop step, merge into the other build, move to Conflicts for Brett, keep. Nothing is changed without Brett's tap. Cheap first pass in plain code (ledger + file overlap); Claude only for the unclear ones.

Correction (Brett): the Sweep does NOT run automatically on every land. It runs only (1) when Brett runs it (button / API / voice), and (2) by the orchestrator on a single build at two points: when it receives the job, and again right before it dispatches it (launches the session). Flags found at dispatch hold the build for Brett instead of launching.

Merged with orchestrator-checks-each-build-against-main-righ for the 'never build twice' part: every build is now checked against main (Shipped features, its PR, its branch, the files its steps create) right before it is queued and again at dispatch; done = closed, partly done = only what is left is queued. before.title: Split builds pages (Build Manager = Pending + Complete; Orchestrator = Queued + Active) with a professional, consistent table design
before.detail:
Replaces one-builds-page-pending-queued-built-tabs-remove (mark superseded).

Pages: Build Manager owns Pending (create, edit, prioritize, Send to orchestrator) and Complete (finished builds sent back by the orchestrator). Build orchestrator owns only Queued and Active (route, assign account, hold, cancel/return to Pending); finished builds go back to Build Manager Complete. Remove every other builds table and the separate Build queue screen (redirect).

Design: polished, professional, like a modern SaaS dashboard. One shared visual language across all four tabs (same spacing, type, badges, row style), but each tab shows what fits it; rows may be two lines tall, info doesn't have to be identical or in the same place. Rows expand to collapsible sections/sub-grids (steps, runs, cost, PR, Brett's words, log tail).
- Every row: dates (created, started, finished as relevant), steps total and steps completed.
- Pending: no timer; created date, steps, priority, Send to orchestrator.
- Queued: queue position, why it's waiting, account/model planned.
- Active: animated activity indicator in the row, live elapsed timer, steps complete with progress bar, current step, account actually running it.
- Complete: started/finished dates, duration, cost, account that actually built it, PR/land status.
Theme tokens only, phone + desktop, screenshots to UI Review. Full API/voice control.

Pass changed path and event type to every action. Log every event and action result. Settings per watch: debounce, recursive, ignore patterns, enabled. List of active watches and recent events. Skip non-essential steps like screenshots (mark them skipped, keep the step).

before.title: Saved Claude logins never end up on a spent refresh token
before.detail: Builds run on a per-build copy of a saved login (claude-login.mjs). Refresh tokens are single-use: when a build refreshes, the new token lands in the copy; if the copy is deleted before the rotation is written back (claude-token-save.mjs release/sweep), the saved login keeps a spent token and every later launch fails with 'OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed' (seen on account-1 and account-3, Nov 9). Fix: find every path where the rotation is lost (crash, kill, exit 1, sweep timing, two builds refreshing the same login at once), write rotations back atomically with a lock, never let two copies refresh the same login concurrently, and before launch check the saved login is alive; if dead, skip that account, alert the phone, and don't burn runs on it. Tests for each path.

before.title: Skins as packages of slices: every section its own asset, pick sections on apply, mix creates a new skin via dialog, drag-and-drop Skin Builder
before.detail: Upgrade the existing skins/appearance system and asset registry; don't build a parallel one. 1) DATA MODEL: a skin is only a package (manifest) referencing section assets. before.title: One VPS plugin: everything VPS in one place (gauges, banner widget with heat-colour icons and dropdown, cleanup, settings, status)
before.detail: ONE VPS plugin (e.g. 'VPS'), reachable from Maintenance and its own nav entry. 1) CONSOLIDATE: find every VPS-related feature across the console and move it into this plugin as tabs or sections, leaving no duplicates behind. That includes the claude-badge VPS check, agent-slots resource and swap settings and warnings, the VPS settings/orchestrator-only rule plugin (from vps-orchestrator-only-rule-vps-settings-console), Docker/container views, container-access, the Coolify/Hostinger links, VPS terminal shortcuts, ai-keys VPS sync, maintenance cleanup/redundancy scans, the disk alerts, and the running-builds watchdog's resource bits. Old entry points redirect to the new plugin. 2) STATUS tab: live gauges and meters for CPU load (1/5/15 min), RAM, swap, disk per filesystem, plus Docker per-container CPU/RAM and the top processes. Several views (radial, bars, compact strip, history sparklines), switchable and remembered, with adjustable thresholds. 3) BANNER WIDGET: a snappable widget for the banner, toolbars and title bars, with modes icon only, icon plus value, or mini meters. It has its own settings (metrics, mode, thresholds, refresh). 4) ICON-ONLY HEAT COLOUR: each icon's colour follows its level on a smooth scale, white (low) to gray to black to red (high). The stops are editable and the theme can override them. 5) BANNER DROPDOWN: clicking any banner gauge opens a dropdown listing every gauge, one row each: a dot in the same heat colour as that gauge, the name (Load, RAM, Swap, Disk /), the percentage, and the actual values (e.g. 9.4 / 16 GB). Rows update live, the clicked one is highlighted, and the footer has Open VPS plugin and quick cleanup links. 6) CLEANUP tab: docker builder/image/container prune, apt/npm/pip caches, journal vacuum, old build worktrees and logs, /tmp, the Playwright cache, and stale git locks. Each has a size preview and a confirm, shows the space freed and logs to the fix log. Optional auto-cleanup over a threshold (off by default). 7) SETTINGS tab: every VPS setting in one place. Plain code, no AI. Full REST, MCP, CLI and voice control. Desktop and phone screenshots go to UI Review.

Build the store module with get, set, unset and list, and migrate existing overrides into the new schema.
steps.why: Schema and migration design for the override store

steps.text: Add a framework-level right-click capture layer, active only when inline edit mode is on. It hit-tests to the deepest child element, builds the parent chain from the token paths and emits an inline-edit open event. steps.why: Changes GUI input handling across all apps

## Brett said (verbatim)
> 

## What to build
Continue build "Server gate: one session per build, no duplicate launches" (server-gate-one-session-per-build-no-duplicate-launches) [orchestrator] — Phase 1, model Opus.
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (5 left, ~2.2 h):
[ ] s1 (~30 min) Server gate: per-build-ID + per-worktree exclusive lock in every VPS launch path; a second launch of a build with a live session is refused, logged, AmberX FYI.
[ ] s2 (~30 min) Fix the dispatcher double-launch root cause (store write erasing the fresh launch record); watchdog reaps any duplicate sessions, keeping the oldest.
[ ] s4 (~25 min) Server gate log: every time ANY server gate is hit (duplicate launch refused, duplicate reaped by watchdog, slot limit, orchestrator-ID gate, main gate), write an entry: time, which gate, which build, who/what tried it, what the gate did. Viewable in the console as a 'Server gate log' page with a count badge and filter by gate; also via REST/MCP/CLI and voice ('show the gate log'). Kept on the server, survives restarts.
[ ] s5 (~25 min) Server gate log banner widget (snappable asset) with count badge showing latest gate hits; tap opens the Server gate log page. Setting for where its entries show: its OWN banner (a strip across the top that only appears when there's something in it) OR any existing banner Brett picks (dropdown of all banners); switchable live; also via REST/MCP/CLI/voice.
[ ] s3 (~20 min) Tests (second launch refused; duplicates reaped; dispatcher no longer double-launches), PR, land through the gate, AmberX FYI when live.
Tick each step: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step server-gate-one-session-per-build-no-duplicate-launches <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link server-gate-one-session-per-build-no-duplicate-launches --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account mossesx-max- for the Opus phase. Tick every step as you finish it (orchestrator.mjs act step server-gate-one-session-per-build-no-duplicate-launches <stepId> done). before.title: Account order (Hulu -> Moses X -> API) + account shown on every build
before.detail: URGENT, boss order from Brett, Nov 12. (1) Account ORDER setting for the dispatcher, drag-and-drop in Claude accounts + REST/MCP/CLI/voice: new builds go to the first account in the order that has a free slot and isn't limited. Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. [ ] s4 (~8 min) Stop opening or keeping PRs as drafts for UI Review: in the push banner's Open PR / auto-PR path, deploy/claude-headless.sh and builds-live/pipeline code, remove any 'draft until UI Review approves' logic and any un-draft-on-approve hook; PRs open ready for review. before.title: Drag anything by API and voice (follow-up to full API control, start only after PR #556 lands): every draggable thing (banner widgets, toolbar items, tabs, dock panes, grid columns/rows, list items, layout slots) gets a move command with drop zones, incl. add/remove/reorder banner widgets; REST, MCP

notes.text: Split by Claude into 21 steps (4 Fable).

origin.said: I want to be able to drag anything on any page, anything that's draggable, I want to be able to drag it. The regular API build land first.

split.note: Split by Claude into 21 steps (4 Fable).

steps.text: Design the drag-move@1 contract: one shape for every draggable kind (banner-widget, toolbar-item, tab, dock-pane, grid-column, grid-row, list-item, layout-slot), with source id, target container, drop zone (before/after/into/side), index and add/remove. Write the spec in framework/spec/DRAG-MOVE.md and an asset-types/schema entry if one is needed.
steps.why: New cross-app contract for how every GUI's drag targets are addressed

steps.text: Write the reference engine framework/core/engines/drag-move.ts: validate a move, resolve drop zones, compute the new order (pure, no DOM), and add an open registry of draggable kinds that hosts register into.
steps.why: Engine internals that every app's drag hosts share

steps.text: Add golden fixtures framework/spec/fixtures/drag-move.json covering reorder, cross-container move, add, remove, invalid zone and out-of-range index. Generate them with gen-fixtures.mts, record the deferred Kotlin twin in PORTING.md, and add npx tsx framework/spec/check-drag-move.mts.
steps.why: Conformance fixtures for the cross-port contract

steps.text: Add the runtime seam in framework/react: a useDraggableHost(kind, containerId, {list, apply}) hook that registers a host with the runtime (rt.drag.hosts) so a move can run without a pointer, and give the existing drag code paths a shared apply.
steps.why: Changes how drag works in GUIs across every app

steps.text: Wire banner widgets into the drag host: reorder, move between banner slots, and add/remove a widget through the banner widget host engine, so it is the same code path as a manual drag.
Wire toolbar items (Toolbars plugin toolbars) into the drag host: reorder, move to another toolbar, and add or remove an item or a dropped hook.
Wire TabGroup tabs into the drag host: reorder, plus move to another group where the host allows it. Also cover the hand-drawn strips that carry data-axf-tab-group (Terminal, workspace panes).
Wire dock panes and layout slots into the drag host: move a pane to a side or into a tab stack, and swap or move layout slots, all through the layout engine.
Wire DataGrid columns and rows into the drag host (column reorder, row reorder where the grid allows it) and give generic sortable lists the same hookup.

Sweep the console and apps for other draggable things (Build manager queue rows, Plan Studio, Pipeline, asset library, banner pop-out) and register each one as a host. List anything left over in the report.

Add the console actions drag.list (hosts and items on the current page), drag.zones (drop zones for an item) and drag.move / drag.add / drag.remove, registered with the full-API action registry from PR #556.

before.title: Server watchdog: orchestrator auto-recovers stuck or killed builds

notes.text: Split by Claude into 21 steps (3 Fable).

origin.said: Brett: if anything stops working, the server/orchestrator fixes it automatically with no one asking. Detect builds marked running with no live session (e.g. killed exit 143, failed exit 1), reset and requeue them, retry failed sessions, keep every slot filled, and send an FYI to the phone for each fix. Never wait for Brett to notice.

split.note: Split by Claude into 21 steps (3 Fable).

steps.text: Design the watchdog@1 contract in framework/core/build-watchdog.mjs. A build counts as stuck when it is marked running or queued-running and has no live session: the pid is gone, the tmux session is missing, the heartbeat (lastSeenAt) is older than staleMin, or an exit code is recorded (143 killed, 137 OOM, 1 failed, usage limit). For each case, define the action: reset the running step, release the slot, requeue, retry on the same or another account, or give up after maxRetries and go back to Pending with a banner item. Also define the recovery record shape { at, buildId, phase, step, cause, exit, action, attempt, account, notified }.
steps.why: New cross-app contract that decides builds@1 status transitions

steps.text: Add the JSON schema framework/schemas/build-watchdog.json and register recovery records on builds@1. This adds an optional `recoveries[]` on a build, which normBuild must keep, plus the journal kind `watchdog-recover`. Old records with no recoveries load unchanged, so no migration is needed. Show this in builds-store verify.
steps.why: Schema + store field design on the one builds store

steps.text: Add golden fixtures for the decision table (killed 143, exit 1, stale heartbeat, live session left alone, retry cap reached, usage limit moves to another account) and a check script. Wire the check into CI.
steps.why: Conformance fixtures for the new contract

steps.text: Have deploy/claude-headless.sh record each run's end: exit code, signal, account and the time it ended. It writes them to the build's run record through builds-live.mjs (and a run-status file under the slot dir), so killed (143) and failed (1) runs leave evidence the watchdog can read.
Add the liveness probe: framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs `alive <build>` checks pid, tmux session and slot heartbeat and returns JSON. Also free slots whose process is gone (orphan slot reaping).

Add watchdog.mjs `scan` (dry run) to the build-orchestrator plugin. It reads the store, finds every running build, probes liveness, applies the build-watchdog.mjs decisions and prints the stuck builds with cause and planned action (--json).

Add watchdog.mjs `run`, which applies the recoveries. It resets the stuck step to pending, releases the slot, sets the build back to queued through pipeline.mjs, appends a recoveries[] entry under the store lock and pushes it live with builds-live.mjs. It does this idempotently, using a per-build lock and a cooldown.

Retry failed sessions. Crashes and kills are retried up to maxRetries (default 3). A usage limit or account error retries on the next worker through deploy/claude-workers.mjs route. When the cap is hit, the build goes to Pending with a note. The retry count lives on the build, not in memory.

Keep every slot filled. After each recovery, and on every watchdog pass, call pipeline.mjs tick while free slots plus Queue work remain. If slots sit idle while the Queue is non-empty, record that as a recovery cause ('idle-slots') and fix it.

Schedule it: add an `axf-watchdog` cron every minute (with flock) to the plugin's install.mjs and remove it in uninstall.mjs. Mount and add the env in the deploy install script. Make the plugin-lifecycle check pass.

Send a phone FYI for every fix. Declare notify type `watchdog.fix` (FYI, low priority) and `watchdog.gave-up` (alert) in notify.json, and send each through axf.notify@1 to the AmberX app with build, cause, action and attempt. Set `notified` on the recovery record and batch several fixes in one pass into one push.

Add the health@1 check 'Build watchdog' in systems-check. It goes red when the last pass is older than 3 minutes or a build gave up. Its auto-fix reinstalls the cron and runs one pass. A gave-up build becomes a banner item with Fix (requeue).

Add Watchdog settings as a section of Settings → Plugins → Build orchestrator (level toolbar applies): on/off, interval, stale heartbeat minutes, max retries, retry on another account, FYI per fix or batched. Stored as plugin settings keys that watchdog.mjs reads.

Add a Watchdog panel in Build orchestrator, built from framework controls and tokens only, in a TabGroup tab. It shows last pass, running builds with liveness, recent fixes (cause → action, attempt, notified) and a Run now toolbar (role=toolbar, aria-label). Each build view shows its recoveries list.
Add the REST API: GET watchdog/status, GET watchdog/scan, POST watchdog/run, GET/PUT watchdog/settings, GET builds/<id>/recoveries on the build-orchestrator server routes.

Add the same API on MCP, the CLI and voice: plugin-commands for the routes (watchdog_status/scan/run/settings), CLI `axf watchdog status|scan|run|set`, the voice/console actions `watchdog.run` and `watchdog.status`, and a console_show / console_open deep link target `build-orchestrator/watchdog` (plus `?build=<id>`).

Write unit tests for watchdog.mjs against a temp store (AXF_DATA_DIR): killed 143 is requeued, exit 1 is retried, a stale heartbeat is reset, a live build is untouched, the cap sends the build to Pending, a usage limit goes to the next account, idle slots trigger a tick, one FYI per fix, and a second pass does nothing.

Add an end-to-end test with a fake claude in HOME/.local/bin: launch it through claude-headless.sh, kill it (SIGTERM, 143), run watchdog run, then assert the build was requeued, the slot freed and refilled, the recovery recorded and the notify sent. Run the notify-control registry test.

Write docs and the catalog: a Watchdog section in the plugin README, help entries, plugin.json/command/CLI-header descriptions for the glossary, and the _claude/builds/README.md recovery flow. Run glossary-index catalog.mjs --check, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars and check-chrome-assets.

Submit the Watchdog panel to UI Review with 3 options (layout variants as assets under plugins/build-orchestrator/assets/), each with desktop and phone shots, in group 'server-watchdog-orchestrator-auto-recovers-stuck - <date>'.

Finish: run all the checks (check-build-watchdog, builds-store verify, check-builds-store, plugin-lifecycle check, tracker --check, the unit and e2e tests). Write _claude/builds/reports/server-watchdog-orchestrator-auto-recovers-stuck.md with before/after and how each feature is reached (REST, MCP, CLI, voice, deep link). Add a THREADS.md row, open the PR, link it with builds-live.mjs link and add it to the merge queue.

before.title: Orchestrator checks Shipped features before splitting any job
before.detail: When the orchestrator receives a job and splits it into steps, it first checks the Shipped features ledger (which must hold every feature the orchestrator has ever built). It must: not build anything twice; not break or redo anything already done; and if a step would conflict with or change something already built, notify Brett (AmberX notification) and wait before going on. Make the Shipped features ledger complete (backfill every landed build) and keep it updated on every land. Also standing rule: ONLY the orchestrator launches builds, picks model and account, owns pending/queue and monitors status; voice/chat sessions only hand it requests.

notes.text: Conflict flow (Brett): a conflicting step is moved to a special Conflicts section and removed from the build; the other steps still build. Brett gets an AmberX notification-panel item that explains the conflict and offers suggested resolutions; he taps a suggestion or types a prompt, which goes to the orchestrator, and the orchestrator makes a new build from it. Then test it: Brett will send a 3-4 step build that deliberately overlaps existing shipped features to confirm the orchestrator catches it.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

Brett (Nov 9): "needs a way to go through all the pending builds and the build queue and search for steps that are gonna break existing work or conflict with it, or it's already done, or it doesn't need it anymore." Add a Sweep: a button on the builds page (and API/voice: 'sweep the builds') plus an automatic run on every land. It checks every step of every pending and queued build against the Shipped features ledger, main's code, and the other pending/queued builds, and flags each step: Already done (shipped by build X), Conflicts (would change/break feature Y, shows the files and lines), Duplicate (same as a step in build Z), Obsolete (no longer needed: superseded or its target was removed), OK. Results: badges on each build and step, a Sweep report with a filter per flag, and one-tap fixes per flag: drop step, merge into the other build, move to Conflicts for Brett, keep. Nothing is changed without Brett's tap. Cheap first pass in plain code (ledger + file overlap); Claude only for the unclear ones.

Correction (Brett): the Sweep does NOT run automatically on every land. It runs only (1) when Brett runs it (button / API / voice), and (2) by the orchestrator on a single build at two points: when it receives the job, and again right before it dispatches it (launches the session). Flags found at dispatch hold the build for Brett instead of launching.

Merged with orchestrator-checks-each-build-against-main-righ for the 'never build twice' part: every build is now checked against main (Shipped features, its PR, its branch, the files its steps create) right before it is queued and again at dispatch; done = closed, partly done = only what is left is queued. Still open here: the check at split time, the AmberX conflict notice and the ledger backfill.

Pass changed path and event type to every action. Log every event and action result. Settings per watch: debounce, recursive, ignore patterns, enabled. List of active watches and recent events. before.title: Saved Claude logins never end up on a spent refresh token
before.detail: Builds run on a per-build copy of a saved login (claude-login.mjs). Refresh tokens are single-use: when a build refreshes, the new token lands in the copy; if the copy is deleted before the rotation is written back (claude-token-save.mjs release/sweep), the saved login keeps a spent token and every later launch fails with 'OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed' (seen on account-1 and account-3, Nov 9). Fix: find every path where the rotation is lost (crash, kill, exit 1, sweep timing, two builds refreshing the same login at once), write rotations back atomically with a lock, never let two copies refresh the same login concurrently, and before launch check the saved login is alive; if dead, skip that account, alert the phone, and don't burn runs on it. Tests for each path.

addenda.said: It doesn't have to be a different job for every single action. Make categories, like a janitor who cleans up all the cache, an artist who makes images, a manager who runs the orchestrator, a builder. ... All the employees' information is gonna be tapped into the old one, right? So everything only exists in one true source, one true place.
We're just gonna upgrade and soup up the old stuff.

So there has to be a back and forth when somebody replies to somebody else. Only if it's a reply, though. If not, it [stays in the same feed].

Open the group chat in a multi-tab group where you can open a new tab with Jim and John's conversation. You can drag an employee from one tab to another to put him in a separate conversation. You can click multiple people and drag them into their own tab. Filter, sort, all that. The employee list needs to show the right thing: ID, their picture, a link to their profile, when they were hired, how much work they've done, etc. And their skills and tools: we have to be able to assign them skills, tools and personas. That's where their personas will be managed. If that stuff is anywhere else, put it all in one place.

You can also assign them jobs or move their job or fire them, and you select from a dialog of jobs and you can add everything you want. It's a sortable, filterable, multi-column, collapsible and expandable rows. Make it sick, dude. Make an HR department that's off the meat rack.

Then give me a meticulous walkthrough that describes everything they can do, everything going on, all the information about them, where it's stored, how it works, and how everything's linked together to the employees. A powerful, extensive walkthrough that even includes every individual setting. Make it 30 minutes. Make it sick.

In the walkthrough, keep the group chat open as picture-in-picture, with the group chat going on while you watch the demo go around the screen clicking stuff. You'll see an alert pop up, and then right in the group chat, John said this or Jim said that, as things go on in the demonstration. Make mock events: a mock build gets done, a mock error is reported, a mock build failed, something being added to the queue or the orchestrator. Make the alerts pop up in the banners and the notifications. Make mock events to demonstrate everything about the human resources department and the employees.

before.title: One VPS plugin: everything VPS in one place (gauges, banner widget with heat-colour icons and dropdown, cleanup, settings, status)
before.detail: ONE VPS plugin (e.g. 'VPS'), reachable from Maintenance and its own nav entry. 1) CONSOLIDATE: find every VPS-related feature across the console and move it into this plugin as tabs or sections, leaving no duplicates behind. That includes the claude-badge VPS check, agent-slots resource and swap settings and warnings, the VPS settings/orchestrator-only rule plugin (from vps-orchestrator-only-rule-vps-settings-console), Docker/container views, container-access, the Coolify/Hostinger links, VPS terminal shortcuts, ai-keys VPS sync, maintenance cleanup/redundancy scans, the disk alerts, and the running-builds watchdog's resource bits. Old entry points redirect to the new plugin. 2) STATUS tab: live gauges and meters for CPU load (1/5/15 min), RAM, swap, disk per filesystem, plus Docker per-container CPU/RAM and the top processes. Several views (radial, bars, compact strip, history sparklines), switchable and remembered, with adjustable thresholds. 3) BANNER WIDGET: a snappable widget for the banner, toolbars and title bars, with modes icon only, icon plus value, or mini meters. It has its own settings (metrics, mode, thresholds, refresh). 4) ICON-ONLY HEAT COLOUR: each icon's colour follows its level on a smooth scale, white (low) to gray to black to red (high). The stops are editable and the theme can override them. 5) BANNER DROPDOWN: clicking any banner gauge opens a dropdown listing every gauge, one row each: a dot in the same heat colour as that gauge, the name (Load, RAM, Swap, Disk /), the percentage, and the actual values (e.g. 9.4 / 16 GB). Rows update live, the clicked one is highlighted, and the footer has Open VPS plugin and quick cleanup links. 6) CLEANUP tab: docker builder/image/container prune, apt/npm/pip caches, journal vacuum, old build worktrees and logs, /tmp, the Playwright cache, and stale git locks. Each has a size preview and a confirm, shows the space freed and logs to the fix log. Optional auto-cleanup over a threshold (off by default). 7) SETTINGS tab: every VPS setting in one place. Plain code, no AI. Full REST, MCP, CLI and voice control. Desktop and phone screenshots go to UI Review.

That includes the claude-badge VPS check, agent-slots resource and swap settings and warnings, the VPS settings/orchestrator-only rule plugin (from vps-orchestrator-only-rule-vps-settings-console), Docker/container views, container-access, the Coolify/Hostinger links, VPS terminal shortcuts, ai-keys VPS sync, maintenance cleanup/redundancy scans, the disk alerts, and the running-builds watchdog's resource bits. Old entry points redirect to the new plugin. 2) STATUS tab: live gauges and meters for CPU load (1/5/15 min), RAM, swap, disk per filesystem, plus Docker per-container CPU/RAM and the top processes. Several views (radial, bars, compact strip, history sparklines), switchable and remembered, with adjustable thresholds. 3) BANNER WIDGET: a snappable widget for the banner, toolbars and title bars, with modes icon only, icon plus value, or mini meters. Plain code. Tests, report, PR.

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-10T20:46:28.820Z

## What to build
Continue build "Open any website by voice on the phone, optionally with the AmberX recorder running" (open-any-website-by-voice-on-the-phone-optionall) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-10 20:46):
"I need to be able to tell you to go to any website and open the web browser with the recorder in AmberX, or in a plugin somewhere."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.

A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.

Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. [ ] s4 (~8 min) Stop opening or keeping PRs as drafts for UI Review: in the push banner's Open PR / auto-PR path, deploy/claude-headless.sh and builds-live/pipeline code, remove any 'draft until UI Review approves' logic and any un-draft-on-approve hook; PRs open ready for review.
