before.title: Orchestrator checks Shipped features before splitting any job
before.detail: When the orchestrator receives a job and splits it into steps, it first checks the Shipped features ledger (which must hold every feature the orchestrator has ever built). It must: not build anything twice; not break or redo anything already done; and if a step would conflict with or change something already built, notify Brett (AmberX notification) and wait before going on. Make the Shipped features ledger complete (backfill every landed build) and keep it updated on every land. Also standing rule: ONLY the orchestrator launches builds, picks model and account, owns pending/queue and monitors status; voice/chat sessions only hand it requests.

notes.text: Conflict flow (Brett): a conflicting step is moved to a special Conflicts section and removed from the build; the other steps still build. Brett gets an AmberX notification-panel item that explains the conflict and offers suggested resolutions; he taps a suggestion or types a prompt, which goes to the orchestrator, and the orchestrator makes a new build from it. Then test it: Brett will send a 3-4 step build that deliberately overlaps existing shipped features to confirm the orchestrator catches it.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

Brett (Nov 9): "needs a way to go through all the pending builds and the build queue and search for steps that are gonna break existing work or conflict with it, or it's already done, or it doesn't need it anymore." Add a Sweep: a button on the builds page (and API/voice: 'sweep the builds') plus an automatic run on every land. It checks every step of every pending and queued build against the Shipped features ledger, main's code, and the other pending/queued builds, and flags each step: Already done (shipped by build X), Conflicts (would change/break feature Y, shows the files and lines), Duplicate (same as a step in build Z), Obsolete (no longer needed: superseded or its target was removed), OK. Results: badges on each build and step, a Sweep report with a filter per flag, and one-tap fixes per flag: drop step, merge into the other build, move to Conflicts for Brett, keep. Nothing is changed without Brett's tap. Cheap first pass in plain code (ledger + file overlap); Claude only for the unclear ones.

Correction (Brett): the Sweep does NOT run automatically on every land. It runs only (1) when Brett runs it (button / API / voice), and (2) by the orchestrator on a single build at two points: when it receives the job, and again right before it dispatches it (launches the session). Flags found at dispatch hold the build for Brett instead of launching.

Merged with orchestrator-checks-each-build-against-main-righ for the 'never build twice' part: every build is now checked against main (Shipped features, its PR, its branch, the files its steps create) right before it is queued and again at dispatch; done = closed, partly done = only what is left is queued. Still open here: the check at split time, the AmberX conflict notice and the ledger backfill.

before.detail:

Pages: Build Manager owns Pending (create, edit, prioritize, Send to orchestrator) and Complete (finished builds sent back by the orchestrator). Remove every other builds table and the separate Build queue screen (redirect).

Design: polished, professional, like a modern SaaS dashboard. One shared visual language across all four tabs (same spacing, type, badges, row style), but each tab shows what fits it; rows may be two lines tall, info doesn't have to be identical or in the same place. Rows expand to collapsible sections/sub-grids (steps, runs, cost, PR, Brett's words, log tail).
- Every row: dates (created, started, finished as relevant), steps total and steps completed.
- Pending: no timer; created date, steps, priority, Send to orchestrator.
- Queued: queue position, why it's waiting, account/model planned.
- Active: animated activity indicator in the row, live elapsed timer, steps complete with progress bar, current step, account actually running it.
- Complete: started/finished dates, duration, cost, account that actually built it, PR/land status.
Theme tokens only, phone + desktop, screenshots to UI Review. Full API/voice control.

before.title: Saved Claude logins never end up on a spent refresh token
before.detail: Builds run on a per-build copy of a saved login (claude-login.mjs). Refresh tokens are single-use: when a build refreshes, the new token lands in the copy; if the copy is deleted before the rotation is written back (claude-token-save.mjs release/sweep), the saved login keeps a spent token and every later launch fails with 'OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed' (seen on account-1 and account-3, Nov 9). Fix: find every path where the rotation is lost (crash, kill, exit 1, sweep timing, two builds refreshing the same login at once), write rotations back atomically with a lock, never let two copies refresh the same login concurrently, and before launch check the saved login is alive; if dead, skip that account, alert the phone, and don't burn runs on it. Tests for each path.

before.title: Skins as packages of slices: every section its own asset, pick sections on apply, mix creates a new skin via dialog, drag-and-drop Skin Builder
before.detail: Upgrade the existing skins/appearance system and asset registry; don't build a parallel one. 1) DATA MODEL: a skin is only a package (manifest) referencing section assets. Every section (colours, layouts, design/visual styles, behaviour, and every other category a skin covers) is its own standalone asset with a name, preview, tags and source. Convert every existing skin into this form, with no monolithic skins left. 2) APPLY WITH PICKS: when you apply, enable or change a skin, a dialog lists its sections with checkboxes and previews. Choose which sections to take and which to leave out; left-out sections keep the current skin's. 3) MIX = NEW SKIN: if the result mixes sections from more than one skin, a dialog asks you to save it as a new skin (name, description, thumbnail auto-captured), with Save as new, Apply without saving, or Cancel. 4) SKIN BUILDER: a slice library (searchable, by category, live hover preview) and a pack template with one slot per category. Drag slices into slots, preview the whole console live, see which slots are empty, swap or clear slots, before/after toggle. Save, apply, export or import as a file, duplicate, edit later. 5) Professional polish: snap animations, slot highlights, desktop and phone layouts. 6) Full control via REST, MCP, CLI and voice (list sections, save section, apply with includes/excludes, build skin from sections, export). Screenshots go to UI Review grouped by screen.

before.title: Drag anything by API and voice (follow-up to full API control, start only after PR #556 lands): every draggable thing (banner widgets, toolbar items, tabs, dock panes, grid columns/rows, list items, layout slots) gets a move command with drop zones, incl. add/remove/reorder banner widgets; REST, MCP

notes.text: Split by Claude into 21 steps (4 Fable).

origin.said: I want to be able to drag anything on any page, anything that's draggable, I want to be able to drag it. The regular API build land first.

split.note: Split by Claude into 21 steps (4 Fable).

steps.text: Design the drag-move@1 contract: one shape for every draggable kind (banner-widget, toolbar-item, tab, dock-pane, grid-column, grid-row, list-item, layout-slot), with source id, target container, drop zone (before/after/into/side), index and add/remove. Write the spec in framework/spec/DRAG-MOVE.md and an asset-types/schema entry if one is needed.
steps.why: New cross-app contract for how every GUI's drag targets are addressed

steps.text: Write the reference engine framework/core/engines/drag-move.ts: validate a move, resolve drop zones, compute the new order (pure, no DOM), and add an open registry of draggable kinds that hosts register into.
steps.why: Engine internals that every app's drag hosts share

steps.text: Add golden fixtures framework/spec/fixtures/drag-move.json covering reorder, cross-container move, add, remove, invalid zone and out-of-range index. Generate them with gen-fixtures.mts, record the deferred Kotlin twin in PORTING.md, and add npx tsx framework/spec/check-drag-move.mts.
steps.why: Conformance fixtures for the cross-port contract

steps.text: Add the runtime seam in framework/react: a useDraggableHost(kind, containerId, {list, apply}) hook that registers a host with the runtime (rt.drag.hosts) so a move can run without a pointer, and give the existing drag code paths a shared apply.
steps.why: Changes how drag works in GUIs across every app

steps.text: Wire banner widgets into the drag host: reorder, move between banner slots, and add/remove a widget through the banner widget host engine, so it is the same code path as a manual drag.
Wire toolbar items (Toolbars plugin toolbars) into the drag host: reorder, move to another toolbar, and add or remove an item or a dropped hook.
Wire TabGroup tabs into the drag host: reorder, plus move to another group where the host allows it. Also cover the hand-drawn strips that carry data-axf-tab-group (Terminal, workspace panes).
Wire dock panes and layout slots into the drag host: move a pane to a side or into a tab stack, and swap or move layout slots, all through the layout engine.
Wire DataGrid columns and rows into the drag host (column reorder, row reorder where the grid allows it) and give generic sortable lists the same hookup.

Sweep the console and apps for other draggable things (Build manager queue rows, Plan Studio, Pipeline, asset library, banner pop-out) and register each one as a host. List anything left over in the report.

Add the console actions drag.list (hosts and items on the current page), drag.zones (drop zones for an item) and drag.move / drag.add / drag.remove, registered with the full-API action registry from PR #556.

Add REST routes: GET /api/drag/hosts, GET /api/drag/zones, and POST /api/drag/move|add|remove, relayed to the open console through the existing remote-command channel. Add a Python validator that matches the engine.

Add MCP tools to mcp_server.py: console_drag_list, console_drag_zones, console_drag_move, console_drag_add and console_drag_remove. Each move is a veto call with a reason, and the read tools are read-only.
Add the CLI command axf drag list|zones|move|add|remove (node framework/cli/drag.mjs) on the same REST routes, with help text in the header comment.
Add voice/AmberX intents ("move the clock widget to the left of the banner", "drag the Logs tab first", "remove the CPU widget"). Each resolves names to ids through drag.list, then calls drag.move.
Add deep links: console_show / console_open targets like drag:<kind>:<host>:<item>, which open the page and highlight the item and its drop zones, plus a state read of the current order per host.
Draw drop zones with tokens only when a move is previewed by API (Follow Amber highlight). Make sure check-theme, check-controls and check-chrome-assets pass.

before.title: Server watchdog: orchestrator auto-recovers stuck or killed builds

notes.text: Split by Claude into 21 steps (3 Fable).

origin.said: Brett: if anything stops working, the server/orchestrator fixes it automatically with no one asking. Detect builds marked running with no live session (e.g. killed exit 143, failed exit 1), reset and requeue them, retry failed sessions, keep every slot filled, and send an FYI to the phone for each fix. Never wait for Brett to notice.

split.note: Split by Claude into 21 steps (3 Fable).

steps.text: Design the watchdog@1 contract in framework/core/build-watchdog.mjs. A build counts as stuck when it is marked running or queued-running and has no live session: the pid is gone, the tmux session is missing, the heartbeat (lastSeenAt) is older than staleMin, or an exit code is recorded (143 killed, 137 OOM, 1 failed, usage limit). For each case, define the action: reset the running step, release the slot, requeue, retry on the same or another account, or give up after maxRetries and go back to Pending with a banner item. Also define the recovery record shape { at, buildId, phase, step, cause, exit, action, attempt, account, notified }.
steps.why: New cross-app contract that decides builds@1 status transitions

steps.text: Add the JSON schema framework/schemas/build-watchdog.json and register recovery records on builds@1. This adds an optional `recoveries[]` on a build, which normBuild must keep, plus the journal kind `watchdog-recover`. Old records with no recoveries load unchanged, so no migration is needed. Show this in builds-store verify.
steps.why: Schema + store field design on the one builds store

steps.text: Add golden fixtures for the decision table (killed 143, exit 1, stale heartbeat, live session left alone, retry cap reached, usage limit moves to another account) and a check script. Wire the check into CI.
steps.why: Conformance fixtures for the new contract

steps.text: Have deploy/claude-headless.sh record each run's end: exit code, signal, account and the time it ended. It writes them to the build's run record through builds-live.mjs (and a run-status file under the slot dir), so killed (143) and failed (1) runs leave evidence the watchdog can read.
Add the liveness probe: framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs `alive <build>` checks pid, tmux session and slot heartbeat and returns JSON. Also free slots whose process is gone (orphan slot reaping).

Add watchdog.mjs `scan` (dry run) to the build-orchestrator plugin. It reads the store, finds every running build, probes liveness, applies the build-watchdog.mjs decisions and prints the stuck builds with cause and planned action (--json).

Add watchdog.mjs `run`, which applies the recoveries. It resets the stuck step to pending, releases the slot, sets the build back to queued through pipeline.mjs, appends a recoveries[] entry under the store lock and pushes it live with builds-live.mjs. It does this idempotently, using a per-build lock and a cooldown.

Retry failed sessions. Crashes and kills are retried up to maxRetries (default 3). A usage limit or account error retries on the next worker through deploy/claude-workers.mjs route. When the cap is hit, the build goes to Pending with a note. The retry count lives on the build, not in memory.

Keep every slot filled. After each recovery, and on every watchdog pass, call pipeline.mjs tick while free slots plus Queue work remain. If slots sit idle while the Queue is non-empty, record that as a recovery cause ('idle-slots') and fix it.

Schedule it: add an `axf-watchdog` cron every minute (with flock) to the plugin's install.mjs and remove it in uninstall.mjs. Mount and add the env in the deploy install script. Make the plugin-lifecycle check pass.

Send a phone FYI for every fix. Declare notify type `watchdog.fix` (FYI, low priority) and `watchdog.gave-up` (alert) in notify.json, and send each through axf.notify@1 to the AmberX app with build, cause, action and attempt. Set `notified` on the recovery record and batch several fixes in one pass into one push.

Add the health@1 check 'Build watchdog' in systems-check. It goes red when the last pass is older than 3 minutes or a build gave up. Its auto-fix reinstalls the cron and runs one pass. A gave-up build becomes a banner item with Fix (requeue).

Add Watchdog settings as a section of Settings → Plugins → Build orchestrator (level toolbar applies): on/off, interval, stale heartbeat minutes, max retries, retry on another account, FYI per fix or batched. Stored as plugin settings keys that watchdog.mjs reads.

Add a Watchdog panel in Build orchestrator, built from framework controls and tokens only, in a TabGroup tab. It shows last pass, running builds with liveness, recent fixes (cause → action, attempt, notified) and a Run now toolbar (role=toolbar, aria-label). Each build view shows its recoveries list.
Add the REST API: GET watchdog/status, GET watchdog/scan, POST watchdog/run, GET/PUT watchdog/settings, GET builds/<id>/recoveries on the build-orchestrator server routes.

Add the same API on MCP, the CLI and voice: plugin-commands for the routes (watchdog_status/scan/run/settings), CLI `axf watchdog status|scan|run|set`, the voice/console actions `watchdog.run` and `watchdog.status`, and a console_show / console_open deep link target `build-orchestrator/watchdog` (plus `?build=<id>`).

Write unit tests for watchdog.mjs against a temp store (AXF_DATA_DIR): killed 143 is requeued, exit 1 is retried, a stale heartbeat is reset, a live build is untouched, the cap sends the build to Pending, a usage limit goes to the next account, idle slots trigger a tick, one FYI per fix, and a second pass does nothing.

Add an end-to-end test with a fake claude in HOME/.local/bin: launch it through claude-headless.sh, kill it (SIGTERM, 143), run watchdog run, then assert the build was requeued, the slot freed and refilled, the recovery recorded and the notify sent. Run the notify-control registry test.

Write docs and the catalog: a Watchdog section in the plugin README, help entries, plugin.json/command/CLI-header descriptions for the glossary, and the _claude/builds/README.md recovery flow. Run glossary-index catalog.mjs --check, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars and check-chrome-assets.

Submit the Watchdog panel to UI Review with 3 options (layout variants as assets under plugins/build-orchestrator/assets/), each with desktop and phone shots, in group 'server-watchdog-orchestrator-auto-recovers-stuck - <date>'.

Finish: run all the checks (check-build-watchdog, builds-store verify, check-builds-store, plugin-lifecycle check, tracker --check, the unit and e2e tests). Write _claude/builds/reports/server-watchdog-orchestrator-auto-recovers-stuck.md with before/after and how each feature is reached (REST, MCP, CLI, voice, deep link). Add a THREADS.md row, open the PR, link it with builds-live.mjs link and add it to the merge queue.

# Build: professional-skins-that-rebuild-the-whole-app-fable-ultrathink-every-step-e

## Brett said (verbatim)
> 

## What to build
Continue build "Professional skins that rebuild the whole app (Fable, ultrathink, every step): each skin is a complete restyle AND rebehave of the entire console UI. Every asset (theme, layout, toolbars, tab groups and where tabs go, buttons and how they behave, context menus, nav menu, app menus, dialogs, tables, " (professional-skins-that-rebuild-the-whole-app-fable-ultrathink-every-step-e) — Phase 1, model Fable.
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (17 left, ~8.2 h):
[ ] s1 (~30 min) Design skin@2, the full design-pack contract. A skin now carries both a look (theme, style, layout, icon pack) and a behaviour pick for every asset type in the registry: tab-group position/overflow/style, toolbar placement and tap-confirm, button behaviour (press, confirm, hold), context-menu form, nav-menu mode (rail/drawer/bottom tabs/top bar), app-menu form, dialog presentation (modal/sheet/side panel/full screen), table density/row actions/sticky header, banner placement. Write the contract in framework/schemas/asset-types.json, regenerate framework/schemas/json/ and document it in framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md. First check pending build skin-configuration-panel-before-ai-makes-a-skin-brett-picks-what-it-may-change (PR #547) for overlap and merge it in or note it.
[ ] s2 (~30 min) Add behaviour coverage to skin-coverage@1. Each registered asset type declares behaviour axes in addition to its look slot or parts (a 'behaviour' block on the registry entry or its style target in customize.json). A type that has behaviour and is missing from a skin is reported as uncovered. Keep it open: worked out from the registry, with no hardcoded list.
[ ] s3 (~30 min) Extend the resolver. resolveLookSkin compiles a skin@2 at every scope (hub, then app, then ui:<view>, then plugin:<id>, child overrides parent) into look tokens plus behaviour tokens (--fx-* and axf.behaviour.* runtime values). runtime.swap('skin', id) hot-swaps both with no reload, and the user's saved per-row overrides (axf.chrome.*) still win.
[ ] s4 (~30 min) Migrate skin@1 and design packages to skin@2. A skin@1 reads as a skin@2 whose behaviour fields default to today's behaviour, and nothing changes visually. Add golden fixtures for the resolve, scope and behaviour outputs, regenerate them with gen-fixtures, update check-skin.mts, and record the Kotlin twin as a deferred gap in PORTING.md (Android is on hold).
[ ] s5 (~30 min) Make the framework controls read behaviour tokens. TabGroup (position/overflow/style), Toolbar (placement, tap-confirm default), Button (behaviour modes on top of the destructive confirm), ChromeContext menus (form), Dialog/window host (modal, sheet, side panel or full screen), DataGrid (density, row actions, sticky header) and the banner host each take their behaviour from the nearest SkinScope. No component hardcodes a behaviour.
[ ] s6 (~30 min) Make the app shell skin-driven. AppShell regions (nav-menu mode and side, banner and toolbar placement, where tab rows dock, menu bar on or off) come from the resolved skin, so a skin can move the console's whole layout. Wire the console's root views and plugin roots so each is a SkinScope with behaviour.
[ ] s7 (~30 min) Author professional skin 1, 'Studio Pro': a dense, IDE-like desktop skin with left rail nav, top tab rows, compact tables, a right-side panel for dialogs and a full menu bar. Covers every registered asset type and adds any assets it needs under framework/assets/<type>/.
[ ] s8 (~30 min) Author professional skin 2, 'Executive': a clean, minimal skin with a top bar nav, pill tab groups, roomy tables, centered modal dialogs and quiet toolbars. Full coverage, plus its own assets.
[ ] s9 (~30 min) Author professional skin 3, 'Field': phone-first, with bottom-tab nav, bottom sheets for dialogs and menus, tap-confirm toolbars at the thumb, card-style tables and big tap targets. Full coverage, plus its own assets.
[ ] s10 (~30 min) Author professional skin 4, 'Command': keyboard-first, with a command-palette app menu, hidden nav drawer, tabs docked at the bottom, inline confirm buttons and terminal-style tables. Full coverage, plus its own assets.
[ ] s11 (~20 min) Bake the shared set: add the new skins and their assets to the shared assets, run shared-assets.mjs bake for the Dev Console, axHub web and AmberX, rebake the console (rebake.mjs apply console-web) and backfill chrome-settings copies where new behaviour settings appear.
[ ] s12 (~30 min) Settings UI: in Settings → Appearance (AppearancePanel), add a skin gallery with live preview cards (desktop and phone), a 'what this skin changes' list showing look and behaviour per asset type, Use skin / Back to skin / Restore to default with one undo, the scope picker (hub/app/screen/plugin) and the level toolbar. Tokens and framework controls only.
[ ] s13 (~30 min) API parity for skins. Deep link console_show target 'settings/appearance/skin/<id>'. State read: the active skin per scope and the resolved look plus behaviour. Actions: use/off/inherit/at/preview/compare/coverage. All of it through theme-manager REST routes, MCP plugin commands, the skins.mjs CLI and voice/console actions (skin.use, skin.preview, skin.behaviour), all four the same.
[ ] s14 (~30 min) CI: check-skin-coverage.mjs fails when any registered type misses look or behaviour coverage in any shipped skin. theme-swap.mjs switches every skin in the built console and fails on hardcoded colours, sizes or behaviours. Extend check-skin.mts and check-chrome-assets for behaviour tokens.
[ ] s15 (~30 min) UI Review: shoot the console (home, builds, settings, a dialog, a table, a context menu) under each of the 4 skins on desktop and phone with rebuild-shots.mjs, then submit them as one choice set of 4 skin options with review.mjs submit --choices. The skins are the assets, and Brett picks them in priority order.
[ ] s16 (~20 min) Docs and catalog: describe the skins, behaviour axes, CLI and actions where they are defined, update the help and the glossary/index (catalog.mjs --check), framework/catalog/status.json + tracker.mjs, and the Skins section of APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md.
[ ] s17 (~30 min) Finish: run the tests (gen-fixtures check, check-skin.mts, check-skin-coverage, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, check-chrome-assets, theme-swap, console typecheck/build, validate --framework). Write the report at _claude/builds/reports/professional-skins-that-rebuild-the-whole-app-fable-ultrathink-every-step-e.md, add the THREADS.md row, then open the PR. The PR says how each feature is reached (deep link, REST, MCP, CLI, voice) and that UI Review is waiting.

Tick each step: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step professional-skins-that-rebuild-the-whole-app-fable-ultrathink-every-step-e <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link professional-skins-that-rebuild-the-whole-app-fable-ultrathink-every-step-e --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account mossesx-max- for the Fable phase. before.title: Saved Claude logins never end up on a spent refresh token
before.detail: Builds run on a per-build copy of a saved login (claude-login.mjs). Refresh tokens are single-use: when a build refreshes, the new token lands in the copy; if the copy is deleted before the rotation is written back (claude-token-save.mjs release/sweep), the saved login keeps a spent token and every later launch fails with 'OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed' (seen on account-1 and account-3, Nov 9). Fix: find every path where the rotation is lost (crash, kill, exit 1, sweep timing, two builds refreshing the same login at once), write rotations back atomically with a lock, never let two copies refresh the same login concurrently, and before launch check the saved login is alive; if dead, skip that account, alert the phone, and don't burn runs on it. Tests for each path.

## What to build

"From now on, you do whatever in your ability to fix any problem... just notify me of doing it, not for permission or veto. Every single build, put that in the brief... anything that's doing anything will be able to follow those rules."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.

Rows update live, the clicked one is highlighted, and the footer has Open VPS plugin and quick cleanup links. 6) CLEANUP tab: docker builder/image/container prune, apt/npm/pip caches, journal vacuum, old build worktrees and logs, /tmp, the Playwright cache, and stale git locks. Each has a size preview and a confirm, shows the space freed and logs to the fix log. Optional auto-cleanup over a threshold (off by default). 7) SETTINGS tab: every VPS setting in one place. before.title: Claude Accounts Manager plugin: one ordered list of every account (subscription + API), usage in dollars, terminal column, banner widget, floating overlay
before.detail: New console plugin. 1) ACCOUNTS LIST: reads every Claude account stored on the VPS and lists each: name/label, email, plan, subscription or API, active builder / active worker / not, out of credits, order number, usage used / total, percent left, plan size; usage converted to dollars everywhere usage is shown. 2) ONE ORDER: drag and drop to set the order; subscriptions and API keys are equal to the orchestrator, it follows the order. # Build: full-api-cli-control-of-everything-plus-an-offli

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-10T16:28:24.043Z
> I need extensive API and CLI control over every single page, app, plugin, tool, behavior, display, and setting with every single option or possibility for a parameter. Need to be able to completely run the console, Molly, axHub, Hostinger, Coolify, VPS, Moshi app, AmberX app. I need a powerful complete index and registry for offline management and internal logic. Anything that can possibly be done without AI needs to be, with AI only as a fallback by default unless you have made Claude available to the console in Claude settings.

## What to build
Continue build "Full API + CLI control of everything, plus an offline index/registry; AI only as fallback" (full-api-cli-control-of-everything-plus-an-offli) — Phase 1, model Fable.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-10 16:28):
"I need extensive API and CLI control over every single page, app, plugin, tool, behavior, display, and setting with every single option or possibility for a parameter. Need to be able to completely run the console, Molly, axHub, Hostinger, Coolify, VPS, Moshi app, AmberX app. I need a powerful complete index and registry for offline management and internal logic. Anything that can possibly be done without AI needs to be, with AI only as a fallback by default unless you have made Claude available to the console in Claude settings."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (3 left, ~1.5 h):
[ ] s1 (~30 min) Design the control-registry@1 contract: one entry shape for everything controllable (id, type page/app/plugin/tool/behavior/display/setting, owner app, where it lives, deep link / console_open target, state read path, actions with parameters, parameter types, allowed values/ranges/defaults, needsAI flag, surfaces REST/MCP/CLI/voice). Extend the ui-api-parity and universal-voice-api-control declarations rather than replacing them. Write the JSON schema, a migration note for existing declarations, and the contract doc.
[ ] s2 (~30 min) Build the registry engine: collect entries from plugin manifests, ui-api-parity declarations and voice intents into one versioned offline index (JSON file plus in-memory query: list, get, search, by owner/type), with validation against the schema, change detection and an export/import for offline use. No AI anywhere in this path.
[ ] s3 (~30 min) Deterministic dispatcher with an AI-fallback gate: resolve a command, CLI call or voice phrase to a registry action and validated parameters using exact ids, aliases, synonyms and allowed values only. Fall back to Claude only when nothing matches and 'Make Claude available to the console' is on in Claude settings; otherwise return the closest registry matches and the gap. Reuse the universal-voice-api-control resolver.
Read first: contracts/control-registry@1.schema.json, docs/contracts/control-registry.md, apps/console-web/lib/ui-api-parity/, apps/console-web/lib/registry/index.mjs, apps/console-web/lib/registry/collect.mjs, apps/console-web/lib/registry/store.mjs, _claude/builds/registry/, apps/console-web/lib/registry/dispatch.mjs, apps/console-web/lib/registry/ai-fallback.mjs, apps/console-web/lib/voice-api/
Tick each step: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step full-api-cli-control-of-everything-plus-an-offli <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link full-api-cli-control-of-everything-plus-an-offli --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

Extend the ui-api-parity and universal-voice-api-control declarations rather than replacing them. Write the JSON schema, a migration note for existing declarations, and the contract doc.
steps.why: Cross-port contract and schema design shared by console, Molly, axHub and the AmberX app

steps.text: Build the registry engine: collect entries from plugin manifests, ui-api-parity declarations and voice intents into one versioned offline index (JSON file plus in-memory query: list, get, search, by owner/type), with validation against the schema, change detection and an export/import for offline use. No AI anywhere in this path.
steps.why: Engine internals: the index every surface and the internal logic reads from

steps.text: Deterministic dispatcher with an AI-fallback gate: resolve a command, CLI call or voice phrase to a registry action and validated parameters using exact ids, aliases, synonyms and allowed values only. Fall back to Claude only when nothing matches and 'Make Claude available to the console' is on in Claude settings; otherwise return the closest registry matches and the gap. Reuse the universal-voice-api-control resolver.
steps.why: Engine internals that change how every app routes actions (no-AI-first rule)

steps.text: Console REST API for the registry and control: GET /api/registry (list/search/filter), GET /api/registry/:id, GET /api/registry/export, GET /api/control/:id/state, POST /api/control/:id/:action with parameter validation from the registry, POST /api/control/resolve (deterministic first, gated AI fallback). Auth and audit like the existing console API.

MCP tools on the same dispatcher: registry_list, registry_get, registry_search, control_state, control_invoke, control_resolve; map token and planner items to control@1 and keep console_show / console_open targets in sync with registry deep links.

CLI `axf ctl`: list, get, search, state, set, do, open, resolve, export; reads the offline index when the console is unreachable; argument validation and shell completion generated from the registry's parameters and allowed values.

Register the console itself: every page, plugin, tool, display option and setting with every parameter and allowed value, each with its deep link, state read and actions; fill gaps found against the ui-api-parity declarations.
Register Molly: pages, behaviors, settings and actions with parameters and allowed values, wired to the dispatcher and the four surfaces.
Register axHub: projects, connections, sync, profiles and settings, with deep links, state and actions; expose the provider bridge used by the next three steps.

Hostinger through axHub: domains, DNS records, VPS power/state, backups and plan info as registry entries with parameters and allowed values, called through the axHub connection (no direct secrets in the console).
Coolify through axHub: projects, applications, services, deployments, env vars, logs and restart/redeploy actions as registry entries with parameters and allowed values.
VPS through axHub: systemd services, processes, disk/memory state, logs, reboot and allow-listed maintenance commands as registry entries; destructive actions flagged and confirmation-gated.

AmberX app: register screens, settings and actions with Android deep links/intents, state read over the existing app channel, and voice phrases routed through the deterministic dispatcher with the gated AI fallback.
Moshi (third-party SSH app): find which deep links/intents it accepts, register only those (open host/session), mark everything else as an uncontrollable gap with the reason in the registry and docs.

Console Registry page: browse, search and filter all entries, see each entry's surfaces and gaps, run actions, and show whether the AI fallback is on. API part in the same step: deep link console_open target 'registry' (with id/query params), its state readable, its actions and filters callable via REST, MCP, CLI and voice, and the page registered in the registry itself.

Parity and coverage checker: fail when any UI page, setting or action lacks a registry entry or is missing any of REST/MCP/CLI/voice, or when a parameter has no allowed values; produce a gap report; add it to CI.

Tests (schema validation, index build, dispatcher no-AI paths and AI gate on/off, REST/MCP/CLI parity, provider mocks for Hostinger/Coolify/VPS, coverage check), write the report with how each feature is reached by deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice, add the THREADS row and open the PR.

What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-10 21:34):

Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.

before.title: Drag anything by API and voice (follow-up to full API control, start only after PR #556 lands): every draggable thing (banner widgets, toolbar items, tabs, dock panes, grid columns/rows, list items, layout slots) gets a move command with drop zones, incl. add/remove/reorder banner widgets; REST, MCP

notes.text: Split by Claude into 21 steps (4 Fable).

origin.said: I want to be able to drag anything on any page, anything that's draggable, I want to be able to drag it. The regular API build land first.

split.note: Split by Claude into 21 steps (4 Fable).

steps.text: Design the drag-move@1 contract: one shape for every draggable kind (banner-widget, toolbar-item, tab, dock-pane, grid-column, grid-row, list-item, layout-slot), with source id, target container, drop zone (before/after/into/side), index and add/remove. Write the spec in framework/spec/DRAG-MOVE.md and an asset-types/schema entry if one is needed.
steps.why: New cross-app contract for how every GUI's drag targets are addressed

steps.text: Write the reference engine framework/core/engines/drag-move.ts: validate a move, resolve drop zones, compute the new order (pure, no DOM), and add an open registry of draggable kinds that hosts register into.
steps.why: Engine internals that every app's drag hosts share

steps.text: Add golden fixtures framework/spec/fixtures/drag-move.json covering reorder, cross-container move, add, remove, invalid zone and out-of-range index. Generate them with gen-fixtures.mts, record the deferred Kotlin twin in PORTING.md, and add npx tsx framework/spec/check-drag-move.mts.
steps.why: Conformance fixtures for the cross-port contract

steps.text: Add the runtime seam in framework/react: a useDraggableHost(kind, containerId, {list, apply}) hook that registers a host with the runtime (rt.drag.hosts) so a move can run without a pointer, and give the existing drag code paths a shared apply.
steps.why: Changes how drag works in GUIs across every app

steps.text: Wire banner widgets into the drag host: reorder, move between banner slots, and add/remove a widget through the banner widget host engine, so it is the same code path as a manual drag.
Wire toolbar items (Toolbars plugin toolbars) into the drag host: reorder, move to another toolbar, and add or remove an item or a dropped hook.
Wire TabGroup tabs into the drag host: reorder, plus move to another group where the host allows it. Also cover the hand-drawn strips that carry data-axf-tab-group (Terminal, workspace panes).
Wire dock panes and layout slots into the drag host: move a pane to a side or into a tab stack, and swap or move layout slots, all through the layout engine.
Wire DataGrid columns and rows into the drag host (column reorder, row reorder where the grid allows it) and give generic sortable lists the same hookup.

Sweep the console and apps for other draggable things (Build manager queue rows, Plan Studio, Pipeline, asset library, banner pop-out) and register each one as a host. List anything left over in the report.

Add the console actions drag.list (hosts and items on the current page), drag.zones (drop zones for an item) and drag.move / drag.add / drag.remove, registered with the full-API action registry from PR #556.

Add REST routes: GET /api/drag/hosts, GET /api/drag/zones, and POST /api/drag/move|add|remove, relayed to the open console through the existing remote-command channel. Add a Python validator that matches the engine.

Add MCP tools to mcp_server.py: console_drag_list, console_drag_zones, console_drag_move, console_drag_add and console_drag_remove. Each move is a veto call with a reason, and the read tools are read-only.
Add the CLI command axf drag list|zones|move|add|remove (node framework/cli/drag.mjs) on the same REST routes, with help text in the header comment.
Add voice/AmberX intents ("move the clock widget to the left of the banner", "drag the Logs tab first", "remove the CPU widget"). Each resolves names to ids through drag.list, then calls drag.move.
Add deep links: console_show / console_open targets like drag:<kind>:<host>:<item>, which open the page and highlight the item and its drop zones, plus a state read of the current order per host.
Draw drop zones with tokens only when a move is previewed by API (Follow Amber highlight). Make sure check-theme, check-controls and check-chrome-assets pass.
Add tests: a vitest/tsx test for each host kind that shows an API move gives the same result as a simulated pointer drag, plus server route tests and MCP tool tests.

Add a Playwright smoke test on the built console that runs drag.move on a banner widget, a tab and a grid column through REST, checks the order changed and survives a reload. Wrap it in agent-slots heavy.
Add glossary and help entries for the drag commands and the drag-move contract, update catalog/status.json and tracker.json, and record the API reach for each host in the help docs.

Final step: run the full checks (validate, fixtures, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, check-chrome-assets, tests). Write _claude/builds/reports/drag-anything-by-api-and-voice-follow-up-to-full.md, add the THREADS.md row, and open the PR, listing how each draggable is reached by deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice.

before.title: Server watchdog: orchestrator auto-recovers stuck or killed builds

notes.text: Split by Claude into 21 steps (3 Fable).

origin.said: Brett: if anything stops working, the server/orchestrator fixes it automatically with no one asking. Detect builds marked running with no live session (e.g. killed exit 143, failed exit 1), reset and requeue them, retry failed sessions, keep every slot filled, and send an FYI to the phone for each fix. Never wait for Brett to notice.

split.note: Split by Claude into 21 steps (3 Fable).

steps.text: Design the watchdog@1 contract in framework/core/build-watchdog.mjs. A build counts as stuck when it is marked running or queued-running and has no live session: the pid is gone, the tmux session is missing, the heartbeat (lastSeenAt) is older than staleMin, or an exit code is recorded (143 killed, 137 OOM, 1 failed, usage limit). For each case, define the action: reset the running step, release the slot, requeue, retry on the same or another account, or give up after maxRetries and go back to Pending with a banner item. Also define the recovery record shape { at, buildId, phase, step, cause, exit, action, attempt, account, notified }.
steps.why: New cross-app contract that decides builds@1 status transitions

steps.text: Add the JSON schema framework/schemas/build-watchdog.json and register recovery records on builds@1. This adds an optional `recoveries[]` on a build, which normBuild must keep, plus the journal kind `watchdog-recover`. Old records with no recoveries load unchanged, so no migration is needed. Show this in builds-store verify.
steps.why: Schema + store field design on the one builds store

steps.text: Add golden fixtures for the decision table (killed 143, exit 1, stale heartbeat, live session left alone, retry cap reached, usage limit moves to another account) and a check script. Wire the check into CI.
steps.why: Conformance fixtures for the new contract

steps.text: Have deploy/claude-headless.sh record each run's end: exit code, signal, account and the time it ended. It writes them to the build's run record through builds-live.mjs (and a run-status file under the slot dir), so killed (143) and failed (1) runs leave evidence the watchdog can read.
Add the liveness probe: framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs `alive <build>` checks pid, tmux session and slot heartbeat and returns JSON. Also free slots whose process is gone (orphan slot reaping).

Add watchdog.mjs `scan` (dry run) to the build-orchestrator plugin. It reads the store, finds every running build, probes liveness, applies the build-watchdog.mjs decisions and prints the stuck builds with cause and planned action (--json).

Add watchdog.mjs `run`, which applies the recoveries. It resets the stuck step to pending, releases the slot, sets the build back to queued through pipeline.mjs, appends a recoveries[] entry under the store lock and pushes it live with builds-live.mjs. It does this idempotently, using a per-build lock and a cooldown.

Retry failed sessions. Crashes and kills are retried up to maxRetries (default 3). A usage limit or account error retries on the next worker through deploy/claude-workers.mjs route. When the cap is hit, the build goes to Pending with a note. The retry count lives on the build, not in memory.

Keep every slot filled. After each recovery, and on every watchdog pass, call pipeline.mjs tick while free slots plus Queue work remain. If slots sit idle while the Queue is non-empty, record that as a recovery cause ('idle-slots') and fix it.

Schedule it: add an `axf-watchdog` cron every minute (with flock) to the plugin's install.mjs and remove it in uninstall.mjs. Mount and add the env in the deploy install script. Make the plugin-lifecycle check pass.

Send a phone FYI for every fix. Declare notify type `watchdog.fix` (FYI, low priority) and `watchdog.gave-up` (alert) in notify.json, and send each through axf.notify@1 to the AmberX app with build, cause, action and attempt. Set `notified` on the recovery record and batch several fixes in one pass into one push.

Add the health@1 check 'Build watchdog' in systems-check. It goes red when the last pass is older than 3 minutes or a build gave up. Its auto-fix reinstalls the cron and runs one pass. A gave-up build becomes a banner item with Fix (requeue).

Add Watchdog settings as a section of Settings → Plugins → Build orchestrator (level toolbar applies): on/off, interval, stale heartbeat minutes, max retries, retry on another account, FYI per fix or batched. Stored as plugin settings keys that watchdog.mjs reads.

Add a Watchdog panel in Build orchestrator, built from framework controls and tokens only, in a TabGroup tab. It shows last pass, running builds with liveness, recent fixes (cause → action, attempt, notified) and a Run now toolbar (role=toolbar, aria-label). Each build view shows its recoveries list.
Add the REST API: GET watchdog/status, GET watchdog/scan, POST watchdog/run, GET/PUT watchdog/settings, GET builds/<id>/recoveries on the build-orchestrator server routes.

Add the same API on MCP, the CLI and voice: plugin-commands for the routes (watchdog_status/scan/run/settings), CLI `axf watchdog status|scan|run|set`, the voice/console actions `watchdog.run` and `watchdog.status`, and a console_show / console_open deep link target `build-orchestrator/watchdog` (plus `?build=<id>`).

Write unit tests for watchdog.mjs against a temp store (AXF_DATA_DIR): killed 143 is requeued, exit 1 is retried, a stale heartbeat is reset, a live build is untouched, the cap sends the build to Pending, a usage limit goes to the next account, idle slots trigger a tick, one FYI per fix, and a second pass does nothing.

Add an end-to-end test with a fake claude in HOME/.local/bin: launch it through claude-headless.sh, kill it (SIGTERM, 143), run watchdog run, then assert the build was requeued, the slot freed and refilled, the recovery recorded and the notify sent. Run the notify-control registry test.

Write docs and the catalog: a Watchdog section in the plugin README, help entries, plugin.json/command/CLI-header descriptions for the glossary, and the _claude/builds/README.md recovery flow. Run glossary-index catalog.mjs --check, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars and check-chrome-assets.

Submit the Watchdog panel to UI Review with 3 options (layout variants as assets under plugins/build-orchestrator/assets/), each with desktop and phone shots, in group 'server-watchdog-orchestrator-auto-recovers-stuck - <date>'.

Finish: run all the checks (check-build-watchdog, builds-store verify, check-builds-store, plugin-lifecycle check, tracker --check, the unit and e2e tests). Write _claude/builds/reports/server-watchdog-orchestrator-auto-recovers-stuck.md with before/after and how each feature is reached (REST, MCP, CLI, voice, deep link). Add a THREADS.md row, open the PR, link it with builds-live.mjs link and add it to the merge queue.

# Build: remove-the-console-s-own-notes-manager-console-u

## Brett said (verbatim)
> Delete the console with no manager. That's whack. Open the Amber X's no manager.

## What to build
Continue build "Remove the console's own Notes manager; console uses AmberX's notes/to-do manager" (remove-the-console-s-own-notes-manager-console-u) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said:
"Delete the console with no manager. That's whack. Open the Amber X's no manager."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (3 left, ~1.3 h):
[ ] s1 (~30 min) The console has its own Notes screen that doesn't show AmberX's notes/to-do items (Inbox, lists). Remove the console's separate Notes manager and make the console's Notes entry open AmberX's notes/to-do manager (same amberx.items store), with deep links to an item (focus by id). Migrate anything only in the console's notes store into amberx.items first. Full API parity.
[ ] s2 (~30 min) Delete the console with no manager. That's whack. Open the Amber X's no manager.
[ ] s3 (~20 min) Tests green, report _claude/builds/reports/remove-the-console-s-own-notes-manager-console-u.md, THREADS row, commit, push, PR
Read first: _claude/builds/reports/remove-the-console-s-own-notes-manager-console-u.md, _claude/THREADS.md
Tick each step: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step remove-the-console-s-own-notes-manager-console-u <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link remove-the-console-s-own-notes-manager-console-u --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account mossesx-max- for the Opus phase. Tick every step as you finish it (orchestrator.mjs act step remove-the-console-s-own-notes-manager-console-u <stepId> done). before.title: Split builds pages (Build Manager = Pending + Complete; Orchestrator = Queued + Active) with a professional, consistent table design
before.detail:
Replaces one-builds-page-pending-queued-built-tabs-remove (mark superseded).

Pages: Build Manager owns Pending (create, edit, prioritize, Send to orchestrator) and Complete (finished builds sent back by the orchestrator). Build orchestrator owns only Queued and Active (route, assign account, hold, cancel/return to Pending); finished builds go back to Build Manager Complete. Remove every other builds table and the separate Build queue screen (redirect).

Design: polished, professional, like a modern SaaS dashboard. One shared visual language across all four tabs (same spacing, type, badges, row style), but each tab shows what fits it; rows may be two lines tall, info doesn't have to be identical or in the same place. Rows expand to collapsible sections/sub-grids (steps, runs, cost, PR, Brett's words, log tail).
- Every row: dates (created, started, finished as relevant), steps total and steps completed.
- Pending: no timer; created date, steps, priority, Send to orchestrator.
- Queued: queue position, why it's waiting, account/model planned.
- Active: animated activity indicator in the row, live elapsed timer, steps complete with progress bar, current step, account actually running it.
- Complete: started/finished dates, duration, cost, account that actually built it, PR/land status.
Theme tokens only, phone + desktop, screenshots to UI Review. Full API/voice control.

before.title: Saved Claude logins never end up on a spent refresh token
before.detail: Builds run on a per-build copy of a saved login (claude-login.mjs). Refresh tokens are single-use: when a build refreshes, the new token lands in the copy; if the copy is deleted before the rotation is written back (claude-token-save.mjs release/sweep), the saved login keeps a spent token and every later launch fails with 'OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed' (seen on account-1 and account-3, Nov 9). Fix: find every path where the rotation is lost (crash, kill, exit 1, sweep timing, two builds refreshing the same login at once), write rotations back atomically with a lock, never let two copies refresh the same login concurrently, and before launch check the saved login is alive; if dead, skip that account, alert the phone, and don't burn runs on it. Tests for each path.

Rows update live, the clicked one is highlighted, and the footer has Open VPS plugin and quick cleanup links. 6) CLEANUP tab: docker builder/image/container prune, apt/npm/pip caches, journal vacuum, old build worktrees and logs, /tmp, the Playwright cache, and stale git locks. Each has a size preview and a confirm, shows the space freed and logs to the fix log. Optional auto-cleanup over a threshold (off by default). 7) SETTINGS tab: every VPS setting in one place. before.title: Claude Accounts Manager plugin: one ordered list of every account (subscription + API), usage in dollars, terminal column, banner widget, floating overlay
before.detail: New console plugin. 1) ACCOUNTS LIST: reads every Claude account stored on the VPS and lists each: name/label, email, plan, subscription or API, active builder / active worker / not, out of credits, order number, usage used / total, percent left, plan size; usage converted to dollars everywhere usage is shown. 2) ONE ORDER: drag and drop to set the order; subscriptions and API keys are equal to the orchestrator, it follows the order. # Build: full-api-cli-control-of-everything-plus-an-offli

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-10T16:28:24.043Z
> I need extensive API and CLI control over every single page, app, plugin, tool, behavior, display, and setting with every single option or possibility for a parameter. Need to be able to completely run the console, Molly, axHub, Hostinger, Coolify, VPS, Moshi app, AmberX app. I need a powerful complete index and registry for offline management and internal logic. Anything that can possibly be done without AI needs to be, with AI only as a fallback by default unless you have made Claude available to the console in Claude settings.

## What to build
Continue build "Full API + CLI control of everything, plus an offline index/registry; AI only as fallback" (full-api-cli-control-of-everything-plus-an-offli) — Phase 1, model Fable.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-10 16:28):
"I need extensive API and CLI control over every single page, app, plugin, tool, behavior, display, and setting with every single option or possibility for a parameter. Need to be able to completely run the console, Molly, axHub, Hostinger, Coolify, VPS, Moshi app, AmberX app. I need a powerful complete index and registry for offline management and internal logic. Anything that can possibly be done without AI needs to be, with AI only as a fallback by default unless you have made Claude available to the console in Claude settings."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (3 left, ~1.5 h):
[ ] s1 (~30 min) Design the control-registry@1 contract: one entry shape for everything controllable (id, type page/app/plugin/tool/behavior/display/setting, owner app, where it lives, deep link / console_open target, state read path, actions with parameters, parameter types, allowed values/ranges/defaults, needsAI flag, surfaces REST/MCP/CLI/voice). Extend the ui-api-parity and universal-voice-api-control declarations rather than replacing them. Write the JSON schema, a migration note for existing declarations, and the contract doc.
[ ] s2 (~30 min) Build the registry engine: collect entries from plugin manifests, ui-api-parity declarations and voice intents into one versioned offline index (JSON file plus in-memory query: list, get, search, by owner/type), with validation against the schema, change detection and an export/import for offline use. No AI anywhere in this path.
[ ] s3 (~30 min) Deterministic dispatcher with an AI-fallback gate: resolve a command, CLI call or voice phrase to a registry action and validated parameters using exact ids, aliases, synonyms and allowed values only. Fall back to Claude only when nothing matches and 'Make Claude available to the console' is on in Claude settings; otherwise return the closest registry matches and the gap. Reuse the universal-voice-api-control resolver.
Read first: contracts/control-registry@1.schema.json, docs/contracts/control-registry.md, apps/console-web/lib/ui-api-parity/, apps/console-web/lib/registry/index.mjs, apps/console-web/lib/registry/collect.mjs, apps/console-web/lib/registry/store.mjs, _claude/builds/registry/, apps/console-web/lib/registry/dispatch.mjs, apps/console-web/lib/registry/ai-fallback.mjs, apps/console-web/lib/voice-api/
Tick each step: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step full-api-cli-control-of-everything-plus-an-offli <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link full-api-cli-control-of-everything-plus-an-offli --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

Extend the ui-api-parity and universal-voice-api-control declarations rather than replacing them. Write the JSON schema, a migration note for existing declarations, and the contract doc.
steps.why: Cross-port contract and schema design shared by console, Molly, axHub and the AmberX app

steps.text: Build the registry engine: collect entries from plugin manifests, ui-api-parity declarations and voice intents into one versioned offline index (JSON file plus in-memory query: list, get, search, by owner/type), with validation against the schema, change detection and an export/import for offline use. No AI anywhere in this path.
steps.why: Engine internals: the index every surface and the internal logic reads from

steps.text: Deterministic dispatcher with an AI-fallback gate: resolve a command, CLI call or voice phrase to a registry action and validated parameters using exact ids, aliases, synonyms and allowed values only. Fall back to Claude only when nothing matches and 'Make Claude available to the console' is on in Claude settings; otherwise return the closest registry matches and the gap. Reuse the universal-voice-api-control resolver.
steps.why: Engine internals that change how every app routes actions (no-AI-first rule)

steps.text: Console REST API for the registry and control: GET /api/registry (list/search/filter), GET /api/registry/:id, GET /api/registry/export, GET /api/control/:id/state, POST /api/control/:id/:action with parameter validation from the registry, POST /api/control/resolve (deterministic first, gated AI fallback). Auth and audit like the existing console API.

MCP tools on the same dispatcher: registry_list, registry_get, registry_search, control_state, control_invoke, control_resolve; map token and planner items to control@1 and keep console_show / console_open targets in sync with registry deep links.

CLI `axf ctl`: list, get, search, state, set, do, open, resolve, export; reads the offline index when the console is unreachable; argument validation and shell completion generated from the registry's parameters and allowed values.

Register the console itself: every page, plugin, tool, display option and setting with every parameter and allowed value, each with its deep link, state read and actions; fill gaps found against the ui-api-parity declarations.
Register Molly: pages, behaviors, settings and actions with parameters and allowed values, wired to the dispatcher and the four surfaces.
Register axHub: projects, connections, sync, profiles and settings, with deep links, state and actions; expose the provider bridge used by the next three steps.

Hostinger through axHub: domains, DNS records, VPS power/state, backups and plan info as registry entries with parameters and allowed values, called through the axHub connection (no direct secrets in the console).
Coolify through axHub: projects, applications, services, deployments, env vars, logs and restart/redeploy actions as registry entries with parameters and allowed values.
VPS through axHub: systemd services, processes, disk/memory state, logs, reboot and allow-listed maintenance commands as registry entries; destructive actions flagged and confirmation-gated.

AmberX app: register screens, settings and actions with Android deep links/intents, state read over the existing app channel, and voice phrases routed through the deterministic dispatcher with the gated AI fallback.
Moshi (third-party SSH app): find which deep links/intents it accepts, register only those (open host/session), mark everything else as an uncontrollable gap with the reason in the registry and docs.

Console Registry page: browse, search and filter all entries, see each entry's surfaces and gaps, run actions, and show whether the AI fallback is on. API part in the same step: deep link console_open target 'registry' (with id/query params), its state readable, its actions and filters callable via REST, MCP, CLI and voice, and the page registered in the registry itself.

Parity and coverage checker: fail when any UI page, setting or action lacks a registry entry or is missing any of REST/MCP/CLI/voice, or when a parameter has no allowed values; produce a gap report; add it to CI.

Tests (schema validation, index build, dispatcher no-AI paths and AI gate on/off, REST/MCP/CLI parity, provider mocks for Hostinger/Coolify/VPS, coverage check), write the report with how each feature is reached by deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice, add the THREADS row and open the PR.

What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-10 21:34):

Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.

before.title: Drag anything by API and voice (follow-up to full API control, start only after PR #556 lands): every draggable thing (banner widgets, toolbar items, tabs, dock panes, grid columns/rows, list items, layout slots) gets a move command with drop zones, incl. add/remove/reorder banner widgets; REST, MCP

notes.text: Split by Claude into 21 steps (4 Fable).

origin.said: I want to be able to drag anything on any page, anything that's draggable, I want to be able to drag it. The regular API build land first.

split.note: Split by Claude into 21 steps (4 Fable).

steps.text: Design the drag-move@1 contract: one shape for every draggable kind (banner-widget, toolbar-item, tab, dock-pane, grid-column, grid-row, list-item, layout-slot), with source id, target container, drop zone (before/after/into/side), index and add/remove. Write the spec in framework/spec/DRAG-MOVE.md and an asset-types/schema entry if one is needed.
steps.why: New cross-app contract for how every GUI's drag targets are addressed

steps.text: Write the reference engine framework/core/engines/drag-move.ts: validate a move, resolve drop zones, compute the new order (pure, no DOM), and add an open registry of draggable kinds that hosts register into.
steps.why: Engine internals that every app's drag hosts share

steps.text: Add golden fixtures framework/spec/fixtures/drag-move.json covering reorder, cross-container move, add, remove, invalid zone and out-of-range index. Generate them with gen-fixtures.mts, record the deferred Kotlin twin in PORTING.md, and add npx tsx framework/spec/check-drag-move.mts.
steps.why: Conformance fixtures for the cross-port contract

steps.text: Add the runtime seam in framework/react: a useDraggableHost(kind, containerId, {list, apply}) hook that registers a host with the runtime (rt.drag.hosts) so a move can run without a pointer, and give the existing drag code paths a shared apply.
steps.why: Changes how drag works in GUIs across every app

steps.text: Wire banner widgets into the drag host: reorder, move between banner slots, and add/remove a widget through the banner widget host engine, so it is the same code path as a manual drag.
Wire toolbar items (Toolbars plugin toolbars) into the drag host: reorder, move to another toolbar, and add or remove an item or a dropped hook.
Wire TabGroup tabs into the drag host: reorder, plus move to another group where the host allows it. Also cover the hand-drawn strips that carry data-axf-tab-group (Terminal, workspace panes).
Wire dock panes and layout slots into the drag host: move a pane to a side or into a tab stack, and swap or move layout slots, all through the layout engine.
Wire DataGrid columns and rows into the drag host (column reorder, row reorder where the grid allows it) and give generic sortable lists the same hookup.

Sweep the console and apps for other draggable things (Build manager queue rows, Plan Studio, Pipeline, asset library, banner pop-out) and register each one as a host. List anything left over in the report.

Add the console actions drag.list (hosts and items on the current page), drag.zones (drop zones for an item) and drag.move / drag.add / drag.remove, registered with the full-API action registry from PR #556.

Add REST routes: GET /api/drag/hosts, GET /api/drag/zones, and POST /api/drag/move|add|remove, relayed to the open console through the existing remote-command channel. Add a Python validator that matches the engine.

Add MCP tools to mcp_server.py: console_drag_list, console_drag_zones, console_drag_move, console_drag_add and console_drag_remove. Each move is a veto call with a reason, and the read tools are read-only.
Add the CLI command axf drag list|zones|move|add|remove (node framework/cli/drag.mjs) on the same REST routes, with help text in the header comment.
Add voice/AmberX intents ("move the clock widget to the left of the banner", "drag the Logs tab first", "remove the CPU widget"). Each resolves names to ids through drag.list, then calls drag.move.
Add deep links: console_show / console_open targets like drag:<kind>:<host>:<item>, which open the page and highlight the item and its drop zones, plus a state read of the current order per host.
Draw drop zones with tokens only when a move is previewed by API (Follow Amber highlight). Make sure check-theme, check-controls and check-chrome-assets pass.
Add tests: a vitest/tsx test for each host kind that shows an API move gives the same result as a simulated pointer drag, plus server route tests and MCP tool tests.

Add a Playwright smoke test on the built console that runs drag.move on a banner widget, a tab and a grid column through REST, checks the order changed and survives a reload. Wrap it in agent-slots heavy.
Add glossary and help entries for the drag commands and the drag-move contract, update catalog/status.json and tracker.json, and record the API reach for each host in the help docs.

Final step: run the full checks (validate, fixtures, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, check-chrome-assets, tests). Write _claude/builds/reports/drag-anything-by-api-and-voice-follow-up-to-full.md, add the THREADS.md row, and open the PR, listing how each draggable is reached by deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice.

before.title: Server watchdog: orchestrator auto-recovers stuck or killed builds

notes.text: Split by Claude into 21 steps (3 Fable).

origin.said: Brett: if anything stops working, the server/orchestrator fixes it automatically with no one asking. Detect builds marked running with no live session (e.g. killed exit 143, failed exit 1), reset and requeue them, retry failed sessions, keep every slot filled, and send an FYI to the phone for each fix. Never wait for Brett to notice.

split.note: Split by Claude into 21 steps (3 Fable).

steps.text: Design the watchdog@1 contract in framework/core/build-watchdog.mjs. A build counts as stuck when it is marked running or queued-running and has no live session: the pid is gone, the tmux session is missing, the heartbeat (lastSeenAt) is older than staleMin, or an exit code is recorded (143 killed, 137 OOM, 1 failed, usage limit). For each case, define the action: reset the running step, release the slot, requeue, retry on the same or another account, or give up after maxRetries and go back to Pending with a banner item. Also define the recovery record shape { at, buildId, phase, step, cause, exit, action, attempt, account, notified }.
steps.why: New cross-app contract that decides builds@1 status transitions

steps.text: Add the JSON schema framework/schemas/build-watchdog.json and register recovery records on builds@1. steps.text: Add golden fixtures for the decision table (killed 143, exit 1, stale heartbeat, live session left alone, retry cap reached, usage limit moves to another account) and a check script. Wire the check into CI.
