before.title: Prompting engine with control panel (events, macros, pipelines)
before.detail:
A general prompting/rules engine with its own control panel (console plugin), built on the decision dialog (build decision-dialog-ui-review-other).
- Create 'prompt events': a trigger (any console/axHub/build event: UI Review submitted, build failed, merge clash, approval held, schedule, voice phrase, webhook, custom), conditions, and what to ask Brett (approve/deny, veto countdown, pick from options, text input).
- Actions on each answer: run tools (MCP/axHub/console commands), macros (saved sequences of commands), or orchestrator pipelines; chain events.
- Control panel to list, create, edit, enable/disable, test-fire and see history of events; templates for common ones.
- Reachable by REST/MCP/CLI/voice/control@1.
- Schema + manifest for events/macros, conformance tests, audit log, Shipped features.
MODEL: Brett wants Fable for the engine, event/macro schema and contract steps; Opus is fine for UI steps. Brett pre-approves the Fable upgrade for those steps.

notes.text: Queued by console.

Brett's full spec (Fable, ultrathink, high quality - he wants this really nice):
Builder UI: left column = categorized, collapsible tree of every plugin/app/tool/screen (orchestrator, asset manager, etc.). Select one -> pick from a predefined list of actions/commands/events that belong to that thing -> set conditions and parameters -> pick the output type (prompt/decision dialog, push notification, email, text message, phone call to Brett, new orchestrator build, delete/archive a build, run a tool/macro/pipeline...). Every choice is context-aware: each list only offers what is valid given everything already selected (dependent, related options; pick builds etc. from live lists).
Triggers include watchdog events (fire on watchdog/health/failure events), schedules, and any app event.
Highly integrated, extremely robust rules + conditions engine (AND/OR groups, thresholds, cooldowns, dedupe, retries, dry-run/test-fire, history, audit). Every plugin registers its events/actions/conditions with the engine via a manifest so new plugins plug in automatically.
Outputs needing third-party services (email, SMS, voice call) via axHub connectors; if a key/service is missing, show it as a 'keys needed' item.

before.title: Transparency token works on every dialog and settings window
before.detail:
Root cause: --fx-opacity-glass / opacityGlass only applies where a component's customization has glass:true (framework/core/engines/customize.ts case 'glass'). Settings dialogs and most panels never set it, so the transparency token does nothing there.
Fix: every dialog, settings interface, panel, popover and floating surface uses a token-driven glass background by default (surface mixed with opacityGlass + blur). Add per-surface-type tokens (glass on/off and opacity per surface type: dialog, settings, panel, menu, toolbar, banner) in tokens.style, editable in Token Control and per instance in Quick settings. Rule: everything visual is driven by a token; add a check that fails on hard-coded backgrounds/opacity. Follows skins. Tests, Shipped features.

Fix: every dialog, settings interface, panel and floating surface gets a 'glass' token-driven background by default (surface mixed with opacityGlass + blur), controllable per surface type via tokens (e.g. glass on/off per surface, opacity per surface), and per instance in Quick settings. before.title: Quick settings: pinned, collapsible pane at the top of every settings interface
before.detail:
Every settings interface (console Settings, plugin settings, chrome settings for tab groups/toolbars/banners/nav/menu bar, and future ones - framework default, enforced by a check) gets a 'Quick settings' pane at the very top:
- Pinned: does not scroll; everything else scrolls underneath it.
- Collapses vertically with a small handle/arrow button; the handle style is configurable in settings; collapsed state remembered.
- Contents, in order: (1) Skin: shows the current skin; checkbox 'Override console skin' to apply a different skin to just this interface. (2) Default assets for this interface (navigation menu, toolbar, tab group, settings interface, etc.): shows the current asset for each; picker greyed out until 'Override console default' is ticked. (3) Override notice: when anything here overrides the skin or console defaults, show 'This is overriding the current skin/defaults' and reuse the existing 'N assets are controlled by their own settings' (chrome.edits) line that expands to list every override, each with reset.
- Any picked asset must have a manifest and pass schema conformance before applying.
- Reachable by REST/MCP/CLI/voice/control@1. Tests, help entries, Shipped features.
Works together with the 'all settings interfaces open in a floating dialog' and per-instance settings-window picker builds.

- Collapsed: a row showing the setting's name and current value, with a small arrow.
- Tap the arrow (or row): the row expands with an animation into a subgrid of all options (cards/tiles, can show previews), pushing content below down; no floating dropdown.
- Tap an option once: it is selected/highlighted (preview where possible).
- Tap the same option again: applies it and the subgrid animates closed.
- Animation uses motion tokens; respects reduced-motion; keyboard and screen-reader accessible.
- Make it the framework default for every select/dropdown control, existing and future (migrate all current dropdowns, add a check that fails on new raw dropdowns). Ship 3 design options to UI Review.
- Asset schema + manifest + conformance tests; skinnable via tokens; reachable by REST/MCP/CLI/voice/control@1.
- Shipped features entry.

before.title: VPS builds get the console token so UI Review works, banner alert when it fails
before.detail:
Headless builds on the VPS have no AXF_TOKEN / AXF_CONSOLE_URL, so UI Review submits are refused and screenshots stay stuck in worktrees, silently.
1. Launcher (claude-headless.sh / dispatcher / agent-slots) passes AXF_CONSOLE_URL and a scoped build console token (vault, never logged) into every build session.
2. Headless screenshot tool authenticates to console/axHub (fix 'Waiting for axHub' and 401).
3. Any failed UI Review submit, missing token, or stuck shots raises a banner alert immediately (errors banner).
4. Re-submit stuck shots found in /root/axf-builds and /root/axf-review-shots.
5. Remove the duplicate pending item builds-get-console-token-banner-alert (filed without an id).
6. Tests, Shipped features.

before.title: Transparency token works on every dialog and settings window
before.detail:
Root cause: --fx-opacity-glass / opacityGlass only applies where a component's customization has glass:true (framework/core/engines/customize.ts case 'glass'). Settings dialogs and most panels never set it, so the transparency token does nothing there.
Fix: every dialog, settings interface, panel, popover and floating surface uses a token-driven glass background by default (surface mixed with opacityGlass + blur). Add per-surface-type tokens (glass on/off and opacity per surface type: dialog, settings, panel, menu, toolbar, banner) in tokens.style, editable in Token Control and per instance in Quick settings. Rule: everything visual is driven by a token; add a check that fails on hard-coded backgrounds/opacity. Follows skins. Tests, Shipped features.

notes.text: Queued by console.

Brett: every surface must READ the glass/transparency token (wired in everywhere, always), even if it doesn't apply it. Whether a surface actually goes see-through is its own per-surface/per-instance switch (on/off), not missing wiring.

CORRECTION from Brett (replaces the previous note): NO on/off switch. Every surface reads its own transparency token value; the default value is 100% (fully opaque/visible). To make a surface see-through you lower its value. Per surface type tokens in tokens.style, overridable per instance (Quick settings).
